隆慶五年進士登科錄

玉音

隆慶五年三月初九日，禮部尚書臣潘晟等於皇極門奏為科舉事：會試天下舉人，取中四百名。本年三月十五日殿試，合擬讀卷官及執事等官，少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、中極殿大學士李春芳等六十二員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates for the Fifth Year of Longqing (1571)

Imperial Words

On the ninth day of the third month of the fifth year of Longqing, your servant Pan Sheng, Minister of Rites, and others submitted the following memorial at Huangji Gate concerning the civil-service examinations: “The Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the realm has selected four hundred successful candidates. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we should nominate sixty-two officials as readers and other officiating personnel, including Li Chunfang, Junior Preceptor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of Zhongji Hall. The grades of status conferred upon the metropolitan graduates shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao. The first class shall, according to precedent, comprise three men: the first shall receive rank 6b, and the second and third rank 7a, with the distinction ‘jinshi with honors’ conferred upon them. Those in the second class shall receive rank 7b and the distinction ‘of jinshi background’; those in the third class shall receive rank 8a and the distinction ‘of equivalent jinshi background.’” The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Readers

Li Chunfang was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Preceptor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of Zhongji Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year (1547).〕

Gao Gong was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Junior Preceptor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of Jianji Hall, in charge of the affairs of the Ministry of Personnel. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year (1541).〕

Zhang Juzheng was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of Jianji Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year (1547).〕

Yin Shidan was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Junior Guardian, concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of Wuying Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year (1547).〕

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the fifth year of Longqing (1571), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. His Majesty took his seat in the Huangji Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, the civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. That day, the Embroidered Uniform Guard arrayed the ceremonial insignia along the vermilion steps and within the vermilion courtyard. His Majesty took his seat in the Huangji Hall, and officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the successful candidates’ names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow results placard, led by drums and music, out through Chang’an Left Gate. Once the placard had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with a ceremonial canopy and retinue.

On the nineteenth day of the third month…

translation_en:
…An imperial banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, court robes, a cap, and a belt were bestowed upon the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan), and paper currency upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial of thanks for imperial favor.
On the twenty-third day of the third month, the first-place graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite (shicai).
The Ministry of Rites memorialized the throne, requesting that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe the graduates’ names upon it.

張元忭〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字子藎，行二十七，年三十四，十月十八日生〕。曾祖宗盛，祖詔〔贈吏部主事〕，父天復〔行太僕寺卿〕，母劉氏〔封安人〕。具慶下。兄元善〔判官〕、元聰、元慶〔監生〕、元思，弟元愷〔監生〕、元愉、元懷、元恂。娶王氏。浙江鄉試第六十八名，會試第一百二十五名。

劉瑊〔貫直隸蘇州衛籍，江西峽江縣人，國子生，治易經，字玉膚，行一，年四十一，二月十八日生〕。曾祖綱，祖佃〔歲貢生〕，父遠〔按察司經歷〕，母郭氏。永感下。娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第七十一名，會試第一百七名。

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the distinction of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Zhang Yuanbian 張元忭, registered in a civilian household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zijin; he ranked twenty-seventh in his family’s birth order and was thirty-four years old, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zongsheng; his grandfather, Zhao, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel; his father, Tianfu, served as Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; and his mother, née Liu, held the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuanshan, an Administrative Assistant; Yuancong; Yuanqing, a student of the Directorate of Education; and Yuansi. His younger brothers were Yuankai, a student of the Directorate of Education; Yuanyu; Yuanhuai; and Yuanxun. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jian 劉瑊, registered with the Suzhou Guard in Zhili and originally from Xiajiang County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yufu; he ranked first in his family’s birth order and was forty-one years old, born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather, Dian, was an annual tribute student; his father, Yuan, was a Registrar in a Provincial Surveillance Commission; and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Yizan 鄧以讚, registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rude; he ranked fifth in his family’s birth order and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Fu, held an honorary official title bestowed for longevity; his grandfather was Lang; his father was Yan; and his mother was née Gong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yijian; Yigao, a tribute scholar; Yicheng; and Yizhao. His younger brother was Yimo. He married a woman née Yao. He placed thirtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

施策〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣醫籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字懋揚，行一，年三十二，十二月十九日生〕。曾祖盛，祖恩〔醫學訓科〕，父教〔醫學訓科〕，母陳氏。慈侍下，兄陽得〔戶部主事〕、夢龍〔知州〕，娶盛氏。應天府鄉試第七十名，會試第二百八名。

translation_en:
Second Class: seventy-seven men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Zhao Pengcheng, courtesy name Rutu, was registered in an artisan household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-eight years old, born on the second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Rong was a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Xian; and his father was Zichun. His mother was née Bao, and his stepmother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His elder brother Yuncheng was a Department Magistrate. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née He. He placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and 343rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Ce, courtesy name Maoyang, was registered in a medical household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather En and father Jiao were Medical Instructors. His mother was née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yangde, a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and Menglong, a Department Magistrate. He married a woman née Sheng. He placed seventieth in the Yingtian Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Yumin, courtesy name Nefu, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the prefectural Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather, whose name is transcribed as 𨥥 [?], was a Steward [the preceding character 日 is unclear] and was posthumously granted the title of Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Left. His grandfather Bingzhong was a Department Vice Magistrate and received successive posthumous grants culminating in the title of Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Left. His father Xikui was Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Left in Shandong and was advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Comprehensive Service. His mother, née Zhang, was granted the title of Lady. Both parents were living. His elder brother Yushi was a Ceremonial Consort, and his younger brother was Yupu. He married a woman née Li. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
劉臺〔貫江西吉安府安福縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字國基，行一，年三十四，正月二十一日生〕。曾祖文詔〔知縣〕，祖敬夫，父震龍〔冠帶生員〕，母李氏。具慶下，弟塾、塋、璧、星、堂、笙、康，娶郭氏。江西鄉試第四十六名，會試第七名。

李際寅〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣軍籍，江西南豐縣人，晉江縣學生，治易經，字寅甫，行三，年二十八，正月二十二日生〕。曾祖秉紀，祖興，父維茂，母蔡氏。慈侍下，兄際春、際東，娶孫氏。福建鄉試第六十八名，會試第三百八十三名。

楊材〔貫湖廣鄖陽府房縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字楚良，行三，年三十，十二月二十日生〕。曾祖顯爵〔教諭〕，祖軏，父薰〔紀善〕，母梁氏。具慶下，兄來，弟朮、采、柬、東、棗、櫜，娶歐陽氏。湖廣鄉試第十八名，會試第五十一名。

陳詔〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字宣卿，行五，年三十，十一月二十六日生〕。曾祖初〔教諭〕，祖相，父文江，母田氏。永感下，兄韶、昭、〔思孟〕、〔思謹〕，弟〔思佐〕、〔思誠，進士〕、〔思賢〕、〔思忠〕，娶張氏。福建鄉試第五十二名，會試第二百四十五名。
translation_en:
Liu Tai, registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Guoji; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhao, a Magistrate; his grandfather was Jingfu; his father was Zhenlong, a government student awarded the cap and sash; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shu, Ying, Bi, Xing, Tang, Sheng, and Kang. He married a woman née Guo. He placed forty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jiyin, registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was originally from Nanfeng County, Jiangxi. He was a Jinjiang county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yinfu; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bingji, his grandfather was Xing, his father was Weimao, and his mother was née Cai. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jichun and Jidong. He married a woman née Sun. He placed sixty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 383rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Cai, registered in a civilian household in Fang County, Yunyang Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chuliang; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xianjue, an Instructor; his grandfather was Yue; his father was Xun, an Admonisher; and his mother was née Liang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Lai, and his younger brothers were Shu, Cai, Jian, Dong, Zao, and Gao. He married a woman née Ouyang. He placed eighteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhao, registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xuanqing; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chu, an Instructor; his grandfather was Xiang; his father was Wenjiang; and his mother was née Tian. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shao, Zhao, Simeng, and Sijin; his younger brothers were Sizuo, Sicheng, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), Sixian, and Sizhong. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Geng Dingli, courtesy name Zijian, was registered in a military household in Huang’an County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and was a native of Macheng County; he was a student of the Macheng County school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiyong; his grandfather, Dazhen; his father, Jin, received the honorary title of Investigating Censor; and his mother, née Qin, received the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dingxiang, formerly Left Assistant Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, and Dingli (定理); his younger brother was Dingyu. He married a woman née Zhu and ranked eightieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Ne, courtesy name Minshu, was registered in an officer household of Tongguan Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Dingyuan County in Zhili; he was a student of the National University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the eighteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhen, was a Vice Commander who received the honorary title of General Who Cherishes the Distant (Huaiyuan Jiangjun); his grandfather, Ding, was an Assistant Regional Military Commissioner who received the honorary title of General of Manifest Valor (Zhaoyong Jiangjun); and his father, De, was a Regional Military Commissioner who received the same honorary title. His father’s former wife, née Peng, was posthumously granted the title of Lady (shuren), and his mother, née Liu, received that title during her lifetime. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yu, Qian, a Regional Commander, and Rang, a military provincial graduate; his younger brother was Lun. He married a woman née Zhang and ranked sixteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yicai, courtesy name Yicheng, was registered in a civilian household in Tong’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian; he was a student of the National University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congzhou; his grandfather, Gang; his father, Duan; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yizhu and Yizhen. He married a woman née Ye and ranked fifty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Maode, courtesy name Jingfu, was registered in a military household in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi; he was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Lian, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his father was Hua; his mother was née Xu; and his stepmother was née Rao. Parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Maoguan, Maocheng, Maogong, Maoxue, Maoxiao, Maozhong, and Maozhen. He married a woman née He and ranked nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Ke 史鈳 was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Ruhe and was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-one, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Jian was posthumously granted the title of Assistant Prefect; his grandfather E was a Vice Prefect; his father Gui was an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Guan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin, a County Registrar, Zhong, and Quan, a tribute student; his younger brothers were Kai, Yuanxi, a tribute student, and Xuan. His wife was née Shao. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Hongxian 黃洪憲 was registered in a military household of the Jiaxing Defense Thousand-household Office in Zhejiang and was a native of Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Maozhong and was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Sheng was an Office Manager in the Ministry of Rites. His grandfather Henian was posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of War and subsequently the rank of Grand Master for Constitutional Service and the title of Prefect. His father Zong was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His mother, née Ye, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace and subsequently Lady of Respect; his stepmother, née Lu, was granted the title of Lady of Peace and subsequently Lady of Respect. Both parents were living. His elder brother Hongye and younger brother Hongdu were Imperial University students; his other younger brothers were Hongde, Hongxuan, and Hongshao. His wife was née Shen. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Shipin 曹時聘 was registered in a military household in Huolu County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Zanhuang County government school specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Xiyin and was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yu held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his grandfather Fang was a Medical Instructor; his father Chun was a tribute student; and his mother was née Gao. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Shiju, Shiqing, Shiyan, Shizheng, Shimao, Shixuan, Shilin, Shi[?] (時の), Shiyue, Shisheng, and Shiming. His wife was née Zhang; his subsequent wife was née Jiao. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Canlu 趙參魯 was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zongchuan and was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongying; his grandfather was Rui; his father Long was an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Sun; and his stepmother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Xu. He placed sixtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Laixian, registered in a banner household of Lin’an Guard, Yunnan, was a native of Hefei County in the directly administered region and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yuande. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the fifth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather was Hua; his father was Haoyi, who held an honorary longevity title; and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Laihe, Laibin, Laipin, Laiwen, and Laixun. His wife was née Ren. He placed nineteenth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Yang was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Sishan. He ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shechang; his grandfather was Jingying; his father was Congben; and his mother was née Huang. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Zhong and Heng. His wife was née Hong. He placed twelfth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhongxing, registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a native of Yixing County and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Zidao. He ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather was Li, granted the title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Xing, Assistant Director of the Office of Imperial Seals. His father’s former wife, née Du, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace; his mother, née Duan, was granted the title Lady of Peace. His mother alone was living. His elder brother Kexing was an Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy; his younger brothers were Shangxing, an Imperial University student, and Tongxing. His wife was née Mao. He placed 132nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shengchun was registered in a military officer household of Qizhou Guard, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, and was an additional student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Shuyuan. He ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Jing, grandfather Zhen, and father Ru were all Battalion Commanders. His mother, née Huang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Tongchun, an Assistant Commander; Dechun; and Mengchun, a tribute scholar. His younger brother was Jichun. His wife was née Yang. He placed forty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

錢若賡〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字德成，行八，年十九，正月二十九日生〕。曾祖瓚〔按察司副使，贈中憲大夫〕，祖崑〔知縣〕，父鳳午，母倪氏。具慶下，兄若申、若寧、若紀，弟若梓、若任、若寅、若訓、若宸、若襄、若許，娶張氏。浙江鄉試第八名，會試第一百九十四名。

沈應科〔貫直隸蘇州府常熟縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字邦彥，行一，年三十五，十一月十二日生〕。曾祖敬，祖嵓，父學，母陳氏，繼母楊氏。慈侍下，弟應第，娶吳氏。應天府鄉試第六十四名，會試第一百十七名。

潘雲祥〔貫山西寧化守禦千戶所官籍，直隸合肥縣人，太原府學增廣生，治書經，字瑞徵，行一，年二十八，正月初九日生〕。曾祖璟〔正千戶，贈署都指揮僉事〕，祖承爵〔正千戶，贈署都指揮僉事〕，父高〔布政司左參議〕，母王氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，弟雲程〔正千戶〕、雲衢、雲路、雲階、雲梯、雲升、雲漸、雲鴻，娶張氏，繼娶袁氏。山西鄉試第一名，會試第三百七十八名。

李時英〔貫浙江杭州府錢塘縣民籍，直隸上海縣人，錢塘縣學附學生，治易經，字含之，行一，年二十七，十一月初五日生〕。曾祖全，祖紀，父方〔冠帶醫士〕，母莫氏。具慶下，兄時芹，弟時華、時蕃，娶邵氏。浙江鄉試第七十八名，會試第十一名。
translation_en:
Qian Ruogeng 錢若賡, courtesy name Decheng, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was eighth in birth order, aged nineteen, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Zan was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Constitutional Service; his grandfather Kun was a County Magistrate; his father was Fengwu, and his mother was née Ni. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ruoshen, Ruoning, and Ruoji; his younger brothers were Ruozi, Ruoren, Ruoyin, Ruoxun, Ruochen, Ruoxiang, and Ruoxu. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Yingke 沈應科, courtesy name Bangyan, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twelfth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Yan, and his father Xue; his mother was née Chen, and his stepmother was née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Yingdi. He married a woman née Wu. He ranked sixty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Yunxiang 潘雲祥, courtesy name Ruizheng, was registered in an official household of the Ninghua Defense Battalion, Shanxi, and was a native of Hefei County, Zhili. An added-quota student of the Taiyuan Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Jing and grandfather Chengjue were both Battalion Commanders, each posthumously granted the title of Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. His father Gao was a Left Assistant Administration Commissioner; his mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady of Peace. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Yuncheng, a Battalion Commander, and Yunqu, Yunlu, Yunjie, Yunti, Yunsheng, Yunjian, and Yunhong. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Yuan. He ranked first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 378th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shiying 李時英, courtesy name Hanzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Shanghai County, Zhili. An attached student of the Qiantang County School specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan, his grandfather Ji, and his father Fang, a physician authorized to wear official cap and girdle; his mother was née Mo. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shiqin, and his younger brothers were Shihua and Shifan. He married a woman née Shao. He ranked seventy-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

諸夢環〔貫浙江杭州府仁和縣民籍，府學附學生，治易經，字仲希，行二，年三十，四月初四日生〕。曾祖能〔七品散官〕，祖寅〔驛丞〕，父餘齡〔醫學正科〕，母嚴氏。具慶下，兄夢璋、夢儒、夢士，弟夢尹，娶周氏。浙江鄉試第六十二名，會試第二百四名。

姚純臣〔貫直隸蘇州府吳縣民籍，長洲縣人，府學附學生，治書經，字熈載，行一，年三十，十月二十四日生〕。曾祖海，祖完，父怡，母陸氏。具慶下，弟忠臣、良臣、賢臣、名臣，娶朱氏。應天府鄉試第九名，會試第三百王名。

袁昌祚〔貫廣東廣州府東莞縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字茂文，行三，年三十七，十二月初九日生〕。曾祖甫，祖大初，父寵，母李氏，繼母李氏。具慶下，兄昌祉、貢、貫、貴、煥、金，弟烱、燿、昌祖，娶何氏。廣東鄉試第一名，會試第四十五名。
translation_en:
Chen Yichao, registered in a civilian household in Ningzhou, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the department school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zongfu; he ranked sixth in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jie; his grandfather, Youjiao; and his father, Sizhong, an Administrative Assistant. His mother was née Zhou, and his stepmother née Wang. His grandfather and both parents were living. His elder brother was De, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his younger brothers were Yiqi, Yifu, Yijie, Yiyue, and Yijian. He married a woman née Lu. He placed ninety-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 391st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Menghuan, registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongxi; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Neng, a prestige official of the seventh rank; his grandfather, Yin, a Station Master; and his father, Yuling, Chief Medical Officer of the prefectural medical school. His mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mengzhang, Mengru, and Mengshi; his younger brother was Mengyin. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed sixty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Chunchen, registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a native of Changzhou County and an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xizai; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Hai; his grandfather, Wan; and his father, Yi. His mother was née Lu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhongchen, Liangchen, Xianchen, and Mingchen. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination; his Metropolitan Examination placing is recorded as “three hundred wang” [?].

Yuan Changzuo, registered in a civilian household in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Maowen; he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather, Dachu; and his father, Chong. His mother and stepmother were both née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Changzhi, Gong, Guan, Gui, Huan, and Jin; his younger brothers were Jiong, Yao, and Changzu. He married a woman née He. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

任天祚〔貫直隸河間府天津衛軍籍，衛學生，治詩經，字良錫，行一，年三十，七月二十三日生〕。曾祖昭，祖倫，父鐸，母王氏。具慶下，娶何氏。順天府鄉試第十二名，會試第三百五十名。

translation_en:
Zheng Bangfu 鄭邦福 was registered in a civilian household in Shangrao County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an added-quota student at the county school; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Hongchou, ranked sixty-second in family order, and was aged thirty-one, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daotong, his grandfather Fuzhou, his father Ning, and his mother née Lou; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bangfu 邦輔 and Bangxiang, and his younger brothers Bangzuo, Bangli, and Bangqi; his wife was née Gui. He placed twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Jiamo 周嘉謨 was registered in a civilian household in Hanchuan County, Hanyang Prefecture, Huguang, and was a native of Jingling County, Chengtian Prefecture; he was a student at the Hanchuan county school, specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Mingqing, ranked seventh in family order, and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kan, his grandfather Richun, his father Dun, and his mother née Liu; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiayan, Jiashan, Jiaxun, and Jiazhen, and his younger brothers Jiazhao, Jiahui, Jiarang, Jiayi, and Jiayu; his wife was née Xiao. He placed sixty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Tianzuo 任天祚 was registered in a military household of Tianjin Guard, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, and was a student at the guard school; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Liangxi, ranked first in family order, and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao, his grandfather Lun, his father Duo, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living. His wife was née He. He placed twelfth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 350th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Guobi 趙國璧 was registered in a civilian household in Dongming County, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, and was a student at the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Odes, had the courtesy name Ziwan, ranked second in family order, and was aged thirty, born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Jian, his father Laifeng, and his mother née Ou; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Guozhu and his younger brother Guoxi; his wife was née Li. He placed forty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

荆光裕〔貫直隸鎮江府丹陽縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字孝啓，行二，年三十五，二月二十九日生〕。曾祖遵，祖瓚，父輅〔七品散官〕，母陳氏。具慶下，兄光祖，弟光祚、光祉，娶鄧氏。應天府鄉試第七十六名，會試第二百九十三名。

魏雷〔貫湖廣德安府隨州應山縣，民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字子鳴，行二，年四十一，七月十六日生〕。曾祖堅，祖化陽，父嘉會〔歲貢生〕，嫡母劉氏，生母陳氏。永感下，兄雲，娶向氏，繼娶吳氏。湖廣鄉試第八十八名，會試第一百九十七名。

余良樞〔貫江西南昌府奉新縣，軍籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字士中，行二，年三十七，正月十五日生〕。曾祖嗣文，祖孔榮〔贈順天府經歷〕，父茂〔通判〕，母魏氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄良能〔序班〕、良楨〔同科進士〕、良士、良登，娶黃氏。江西鄉試第三十七名，會試第一百四十六名。

李登〔貫陝西榆林衛，軍籍，衛學生，治詩經，字瀛士，行一，年四十二，六月十五日生〕。曾祖景，祖永，父欽〔州吏目〕，母萬氏。永感下，弟勳，娶焦氏。陝西鄉試第三十五名，會試第三百八十八名。
translation_en:
Jing Guangyu, of Danyang County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xiaoqi. Second in birth order, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zun, his grandfather Zan, and his father Lu, a titular official of the seventh rank; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Guangzu, and his younger brothers were Guangzuo and Guangzhi. He married a woman née Deng. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Lei, of Yingshan County, Sui Subprefecture, De'an Prefecture, Huguang, was registered in a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ziming. Second in birth order, he was forty-one years old and was born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Huayang, and his father Jiahui, an annual tribute student; his legal mother was née Liu and his birth mother née Chen. His parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yun. He married a woman née Xiang and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed eighty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Liangshu, of Fengxin County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a military household and was an added student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shizhong. Second in birth order, he was thirty-seven years old and was born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siwen, his grandfather Kongrong, posthumously granted the title of Registrar of Shuntian Prefecture, and his father Mao, an Assistant Prefect; his mother, née Wei, had been granted the title of Lady (ruren). His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Liangneng, an Usher, Liangzhen, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year, Liangshi, and Liangdeng. He married a woman née Huang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Deng, of Yulin Guard, Shaanxi, was registered in a military household and was a guard school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yingshi. First in birth order, he was forty-two years old and was born on the fifteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Yong, and his father Qin, a subprefectural Clerk; his mother was née Wan. His parents were deceased. His younger brother was Xun. He married a woman née Jiao. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 388th in the Metropolitan Examination.

洪烝〔貫浙江嘉興府平湖縣竈籍，國子生，治書經，字惟進，行三，年三十四，八月十一日生〕。曾祖必達，祖清〔聽選官〕，父梁，母陳氏。具慶下，兄燿、爟、灼、照、燈、勳，弟黙、燾，娶何氏。浙江鄉試第十四名，會試第一百四十九名。

吳思學〔貫江西建昌府廣昌縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字叔敏，行一，年二十五，十月初四日生〕。曾祖瑀，祖天俸，父國才，前母何氏，母何氏。重慶下，弟思齊、思敬，娶何氏。江西鄉試第三名，會試第三十二名。

趙範〔貫福建漳州府漳浦縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字範之，行一，年二十八，十二月二十九日生〕。曾祖均，祖克鈍，父叔寛，前母蘇氏，母黃氏。具慶下，弟桎、棣、桱、槓、櫏、彬，娶戴氏。福建鄉試第四十五名，會試第一百八名。

李伯春〔貫直隸松江府上海縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字友卿，行一，年二十九，三月十五日生〕。曾祖觀，祖學〔壽官〕，父得祥〔恩例訓導〕，母陳氏。重慶下，弟仲春、熈春、煦春、叔春，娶周氏。應天府鄉試第一百十名，會試第二百十二名。
translation_en:
Hong Zheng 洪烝, of Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Weijin. Ranked third in his family, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the eleventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bida; his grandfather was Qing, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his father was Liang, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yao, Guan, Zhuo, Zhao, Deng, and Xun; his younger brothers were Mo and Tao. His wife was née He. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Sixue 吳思學, of Guangchang County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shumin. Ranked first in his family, he was aged twenty-five and was born on the fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather was Tianfeng; his father was Guocai. His father's former wife was née He, and his mother was also née He. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Siqi and Sijing. His wife was née He. He placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Fan 趙範, of Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Fanzhi. Ranked first in his family, he was aged twenty-eight and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather was Kedun; his father was Shukuan. His father's former wife was née Su, and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhi, Di, Jing, Gang, Qian, and Bin. His wife was née Dai. He placed forty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Bochun 李伯春, of Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Youqing. Ranked first in his family, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the fifteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Guan; his grandfather was Xue, who held an honorary official rank granted for longevity; his father was Dexiang, an Assistant Instructor appointed under provisions for imperial favor; his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zhongchun, Xichun, Xuchun, and Shuchun. His wife was née Zhou. He placed 110th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

趙秉孜〔貫福建泉州府南安縣，民籍，府學生，治易經，字恆守，行三，年三十三，三月初二日生〕。曾祖魁，祖璘，父大申，母傅氏。嚴侍下，兄秉脩、秉忠，弟秉升、秉章，娶蔡氏，繼娶郭氏。福建鄉試第四十一名，會試第一百四十八名。

裴賜〔貫山西平陽府絳州稷山縣，軍籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字公受，行一，年二十四，三月初三日生〕。曾祖增〔九品散官〕，祖明〔聽選官〕，父禮〔監生〕，母胡氏。慈侍下，娶梁氏。山西鄉試第六名，會試第二百六十五名。

張彥〔貫湖廣承天衛，官籍，承天府學生，治易經，字士美，行二，年三十一，六月二十七日生〕。曾祖傑，祖秀，父瑤，前母許氏，母魏氏。慈侍下，兄京，娶大氏。湖廣鄉試第二十一名，會試第三百一名。

杜搢〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字端叔，行二百五十八，年三十，閏五月十七日生〕。曾祖叔寘，祖欒〔贈通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，父士希〔累封通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕，母李氏〔累封淑人〕。具慶下，兄拯〔通議大夫、都察院右副都御史〕、抃、哲〔歲貢生〕、撰、擢、揭、授、掄，娶雷氏。江西鄉試第二十九名，會試第十三名。
translation_en:
Zhao Bingzi, registered in Nan’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Hengshou. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and born on the second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Kui, his grandfather Lin, his father Dashen, and his mother née Fu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Bingxiu and Bingzhong, and his younger brothers Bingsheng and Bingzhang. He married a woman née Cai and subsequently a woman née Guo. He ranked forty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pei Ci, registered in Jishan County, Jiangzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Gongshou. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-four and born on the third day of the third month. His great-grandfather Zeng held a ninth-rank prestige title; his grandfather Ming was an official awaiting selection for appointment; his father Li was an Imperial University student. His mother was née Hu. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Liang. He ranked sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yan, registered in Chengtian Guard, Huguang, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Chengtian prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shimei. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Jie, his grandfather Xiu, and his father Yao. His father’s former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Wei. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Jing. He married a woman née Da. He ranked twenty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 301st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Jin, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Duanshu. His recorded birth-order position was 258; he was aged thirty and born on the seventeenth day of the intercalary fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shuzhi. His grandfather Luan was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His father Shixi received successive honorary grants culminating in those same titles. His mother, née Li, received successive honorary grants culminating in the title Lady of Virtue (shuren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zheng, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; Bian; Zhe, an annual tribute student; Zhuan; Zhuo; Jie; Shou; and Lun. He married a woman née Lei. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

熊惟學〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字習之，行一，年三十四，三月初四日生〕。曾祖蘭〔知府，贈中憲大夫〕，祖木〔府同知〕，父袤，母丁氏。慈侍下，弟惟思、惟一〔監生〕、惟恭、惟明、惟寬，娶鄧氏。江西鄉試第四十五名，會試第四名。
translation_en:
Guan Zhidao, courtesy name Dengzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-two, born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiang, his grandfather He, his father Ao, and his mother née Qian; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zundao, Daxia, Dayou, and Dadao, and his wife was née Chen. He placed fifty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lao Xunzhi, courtesy name Weimin, was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-seven, born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Lin, and his father Shan, a tribute student; his legal mother was née Lu and his birth mother née Zhou. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Xunxue, and his younger brothers were Xunfu, Xunyan, and Xundao. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently women née Lu and née Tang. He placed 117th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Jizhi, courtesy name Sishan, was registered in a civilian household in Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Poetry, ranked second among his brothers, and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuo, his grandfather Yu, his father He, and his mother née Zhou; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiyin, a County Vice Magistrate, Jigao, Jishou, and Ji’en; his younger brothers were Jishu, an Assistant Commander of the Embroidered-uniform Guard, Jixian, and Jizhen, a student of the Directorate of Education. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Yuan. He placed twenty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Weixue, courtesy name Xizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi; he was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-four, born on the fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather Lan was a Prefect, posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Palace Service; his grandfather Mu was an Associate Prefect, his father was Mao, and his mother was née Ding. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Weisi, Weiyi, a student of the Directorate of Education, Weigong, Weiming, and Weikuan, and his wife was née Deng. He placed forty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Xiu, registered in a civilian household in Wucheng County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a native of Wujiang County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An additional student of the Wucheng County school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yuexian; he ranked fifth in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the thirtieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Cunren; his grandfather, Lin; his father, Ji; his mother, née Zhang; and his stepmother, née Ni. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhongli, Zhongxing, and Zhongfu. His wife was née Sheng. He placed seventy-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shiyuan was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Renfu; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather, Xiang; his father, Zhuo, an Imperial University student; and his mother, née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zeng and Daojing, and his younger brother was Shixuan. His wife was née Lu. He placed seventy-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 385th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Heng was registered in an artisan household in Hancheng County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Daoxing; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Min; his father, Sanjie, who held honorary official status for longevity; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yuan, and his younger brother was Jiusi. His wife was née Wei; he subsequently married another woman née Wei. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gan Yiji was registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Defu; he ranked third in his family and was forty-three years old, born on the tenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather, Gui; and his father, Yuankui, Assistant Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture. His father’s former wife was née Wen, and his mother was née Jin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yipeng and Yifeng, the latter a tribute scholar (gongshi). His wife was née Dugu. He placed eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lü Sancai 呂三才 was registered in Linqu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zican and was listed as first in birth order. He was thirty-one, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng, his grandfather Xian, his father Jin, and his mother née Yan; both parents were living. His elder brother was Sansheng, and his younger brothers were Sanpin, Sanle, Sance, and Sanwei. He married a woman née Gao. He placed forty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zhaolong 黃兆隆 was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in an artisan household. An supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Maode and was sixth in birth order. He was thirty-one, born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, Salt Transport Commissioner; his grandfather was Sicheng, Assistant Magistrate; and his father was Yuanling. His father's former wife was née Pan, and his mother was née Hu; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhaodeng, Zhaozheng, Zhaoying, Zhaoji, and Zhaofan, and his younger brother was Zhaobi. He married a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Youguang 周有光 was registered in Ronghe County, Puzhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Xianbo and was first in birth order. He was twenty-eight, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Lin, his father Chaoyong, and his mother née Li; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Youduan, Youtu, Yourong, Youren, and Yougao. He married a woman née Pan. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 335th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Liangxin 夏良心 was registered in Guangde Subprefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he had the courtesy name Zongyao and was third in birth order. He was thirty-three, born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Song, and his father Xiong, who held an honorary title for longevity. His legal mother was née Zong, and his birth mother was née Liu; the entry records both parents as living. His elder brothers were Liangcai and Liangneng, both Imperial University students. His younger brothers were Liangqi, a county Registrar, and Liangfu, an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Pan. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Yukui, courtesy name Zhiqing, was from Gaoping County, Zezhou, Shanxi, and registered in a civilian household. An supplementary student of the county school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He was first in birth order, aged twenty, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather, Tao, was an annual tribute student granted the cap and sash of official status and the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His father, Chongwen, was a Prefect; his mother, née Zhang, was granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yulong, Yubo, and Yutao, and he married a woman née Guo. He placed fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dengyun, courtesy name Panlong, was from Ningyang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and registered in a military household. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shu; his grandfather was Teng; and his father, Pu, was a County Registrar. His father's former wife was née Ning, and his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lingyun and Buyun, and he married a woman née Hu. He placed sixty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Lianggan, courtesy name Yining, was from Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili), and registered in a civilian household. A student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather's name is recorded as 𤇍 [reading uncertain]; and his father was Rujin. His mother was née Bi, and his stepmother was née She. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lianggui and Lianghan, and he married a woman née Zhu. He placed sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huo Zhendong, courtesy name Yanfan, was from Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and registered in a civilian household. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ren; his grandfather was Jing; and his father was Zheng. His mother was née Deng, and his stepmother was née Liang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingqi, and he married a woman née Liang. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Shineng, registered in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zicai. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzheng, his grandfather Zongxing, and his father Daxiang; his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shifan, and his younger brothers were Shiying, Shiji, Shixi, Shike, and Shiju. His wife was née Li. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Yongwei, registered in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Aixian. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the fourteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather He (a tribute student), and his father Ruqian; his mother was née Gao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Nan, and his younger brothers were Gang, Ying, Pu, Shu [?], and Jie. He married a woman née Dai and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed seventy-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 321st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shang Weizheng, registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Shangde. He ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather Gongze received successive posthumous grants of the titles Grand Master for Upright Service and Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His father, Tingshi, was Chief Minister of the Branch Court of the Imperial Stud. His mother, née Chen, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Weizong and Weichen; his younger brothers were Weishi (a tribute student), Weixian, and Weiyin (an Imperial University student). His wife was née Jin. He placed fifteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guan Ji, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was an auxiliary student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Zishi. He ranked fifty-fifth in his generation and was twenty-eight years old, born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Huai, and his father Kui; his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zhou (an Office Manager in the Ministry of War), Fu (a Magistrate), Jie, Ji (a Registrar in a guard), He, and Fei (an official awaiting selection for appointment). His younger brothers were Qing, Zhun, and Qi. His wife was née Huang. He placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

熊敦朴〔貫四川叙州府富順縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治春秋，字茂初，行十三，年二十八，二月二十九日生。〕曾祖仕廉，祖載〔知州〕，父過〔禮部郎中〕，前母黄氏〔贈安人〕，母翁氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，兄敦艮、友麟〔貢士〕、敦大、敦典、敦宗、敦業〔監生〕，弟敦孝、敦誼、敦禮。娶甘氏。四川鄉試第十七名，會試第三百九十三名。

李時達〔貫四川成都府井研縣，竈籍，縣學生，治詩經，字子行，行一，年三十一，三月初七日生。〕曾祖鑑，祖正珠，父萬策，母王氏。重慶下，弟時遷、時遇。娶黄氏，繼娶曾氏。四川鄉試第二十名，會試第四十名。

王守誠〔貫河南河南府嵩縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字時化，行一，年二十八，六月十一日生。〕曾祖聰，祖振，父京〔壽官〕，嫡母李氏，生母楊氏。具慶下，娶髙氏。河南鄉試第六十九名，會試第三百十一名。

莫與齊〔貫廣西柳州府柳城縣，民籍，馬平縣人，府學增廣生，治詩經，字道望，行二，年二十二，三月初四日生。〕曾祖汝能〔知縣〕，祖大德〔知縣，封監察御史〕，父抑〔按察司副使〕，前母趙氏〔贈孺人〕，母王氏〔封孺人〕。重慶下，兄與京，弟與髙、與尚。娶徐氏。廣西鄉試第十六名，會試第二百六十二名。
translation_en:
Xiong Dunpu, registered in a civilian household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was an attached student of the county school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Maochu; he ranked thirteenth in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Shilian; his grandfather, Zai, was a department magistrate; and his father, Guo, was a director in the Ministry of Rites. His father's former wife, née Huang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace (anren); his mother, née Weng, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dungen, Youlin (a tribute scholar), Dunda, Dundian, Dunzong, and Dunye (an Imperial University student); his younger brothers were Dunxiao, Dunyi, and Dunli. He married a woman née Gan. He placed seventeenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 393rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shida, registered in a salt-producing household in Jingyan County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county-school student and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zixing; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the seventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Zhengzhu, his father Wance, and his mother née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shiqian and Shiyu. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Zeng. He placed twentieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shoucheng, registered in a civilian household in Song County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, was an Imperial University student and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shihua; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the eleventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Cong, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Jing, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity. His legal mother was née Li, and his birth mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Gao. He placed sixty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 311th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mo Yuqi, registered in a civilian household in Liucheng County, Liuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, and a native of Maping County, was an additional student of the prefectural school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Daowang; he ranked second in his family and was twenty-two years old, born on the fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather, Runeng, was a district magistrate; his grandfather, Dade, was a district magistrate and was granted the honorary title of investigating censor; and his father, Yi, was a vice commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission. His father's former wife, née Zhao, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his mother, née Wang, was granted the same title. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Yujing, and his younger brothers were Yugao and Yushang. He married a woman née Xu. He placed sixteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

施天麟〔貫直隸池州府青陽縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字以德，行二，年三十，十月初四日生〕。曾祖潤，祖樟，父藎臣，母孫氏。重慶下。兄天奇，弟天迪、天捷、天彥。娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第九十六名，會試第五十六名。

王教〔貫山東濟南府淄川縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字子脩，行三，年三十二，九月十四日生〕。曾祖綱，祖文，父珏，母尹氏。慈侍下。兄政、敬。娶許氏。山東鄉試第十七名，會試第一百三十九名。

劉元震〔貫直隸河間府任丘縣，軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字衍亨，行一，年二十九，九月二十日生〕。曾祖璟，祖蓁〔贈戶部郎中〕，父勃〔按察司僉事〕，母章氏〔封安人〕。重慶下。弟元翰、元泰、元霖、元冲。娶張氏。順天府鄉試第四十四名，會試第六十二名。
translation_en:
Yang Peixun, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an auxiliary student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Weishi. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was He; his grandfather, Kuan; his father, Luan, a County Magistrate; and his mother, née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Fengxin, Yiren, and Fa, and his younger brothers were Guixiao, Peili, Peifan, Peidu, Peizhang, and Peizhen [the division of some names is uncertain]. His wife was née Huang. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Tianlin, registered in Qingyang County, Chizhou Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yide. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Run; his grandfather, Zhang; his father, Jinchen; and his mother, née Sun. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Tianqi; his younger brothers were Tiandi, Tianjie, and Tianyan. His wife was née Chen. He placed ninety-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiao, registered in Zichuan County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zixiu. He ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather, Wen; his father, Jue; and his mother, née Yin. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zheng and Jing. His wife was née Xu. He placed seventeenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yuanzhen, registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yanheng. He ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Zhen, posthumously granted the title of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his father, Bo, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his mother, née Zhang, granted the title of Lady of Repose. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yuanhan, Yuantai, Yuanlin, and Yuanchong. His wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

周思宸，貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，府學附學生，治《書經》，字進可，行十七，年三十，七月初六日生。曾祖澐，祖理〔王府引禮舍人〕，父如漢〔府通判〕，母王氏。具慶下，兄思濟〔知縣〕、思宗〔監生〕、思充〔監察御史〕，弟思寅、思寰、思賓、思襄、思密、思憲、思家、思衷，娶孫氏。浙江鄉試第十九名，會試第五十九名。

侯堯封，貫直隸蘇州府嘉定縣，民籍，松江府上海縣人，國子生，治《易經》，字欽之，行一，年四十一，十月初一日生。曾祖璞，祖論，父廷用，母朱氏。慈侍下，娶沈氏，繼娶郁氏、張氏。應天府鄉試第六十九名，會試第三百四十一名。

translation_en:
Zhou Sichen, courtesy name Jinke, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. Seventeenth in family order, he was aged thirty and born on the sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather, Li, was a Ceremonial Usher in a princely establishment; his father, Ruhan, was an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Siji, a District Magistrate; Sizong, an Imperial University student; and Sichong, an Investigating Censor. His younger brothers were Siyin, Sihuan, Sibin, Sixiang, Simi, Sixian, Sijia, and Sizhong. His wife was née Sun. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Hezheng, courtesy name Xuanqing, was registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. First in family order, he was aged thirty-four and born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Gui, was a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue; his grandfather, Yao, was a Prefect; his father, Shunzhi, was Right Assistant Censor-in-chief in the Censorate; and his mother, née Zhuang, held the conferred title of Lady. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His younger brothers were Xizheng, Kuizheng, and Fuzheng. His wife was née Wan. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Yaofeng, courtesy name Qinzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in family order, aged forty-one, and born on the first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Pu; his grandfather, Lun; his father, Tingyong; and his mother, née Zhu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His wife was née Shen; his subsequent wives were née Yu and née Zhang. He placed sixty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 341st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Dehan, courtesy name Ruhai, was registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Sixteenth in family order, he was aged thirty-four and born on the second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather, Xian, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Governance. His grandfather, Shouyi, held the title Grand Master of Central Compliance and served as Chancellor of the Nanjing Imperial University; he was posthumously appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Wenzhuang. His father, Shan, was a Right Administration Vice Commissioner, and his mother, née Chen, held the conferred title Lady of Respect. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Deyuan and Dejun; his younger brothers were Depu, Dewen, Dezhi, Deyong, Deji, Dezhu, and Dezao. His wife was née He. He placed ninety-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Minghe 張鳴鶴 was from Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and belonged to a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yugao; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin〔holder of an honorary title for longevity〕; his grandfather was Liu〔holder of an honorary title for righteousness〕; his father was Li, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Minghong, Mingyan, Minge, and Mingfeng. His wife was née Zhu. He placed forty-ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Jiachen 公家臣 was from Mengyin County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and belonged to a military household. A student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Gongfu; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingren〔posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works〕; his grandfather was Jikui〔Surveillance Vice Commissioner〕; his father was Yizai〔District Magistrate〕, and his mother was née Bao. He had living grandparents as well as both parents. His younger brothers were Jiaxiang, Jialin, and Jiaqing. His wife was née Li. He placed second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Third class: 316 men, granted the status of metropolitan graduate (jinshi) by assimilation.

Jin Jie, registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zisheng; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-nine, born on the ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Ming, and his father Luan; his mother was née Shao and his stepmother née Zhan. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Ji, Ling, and Sheng, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 314th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Liangyin, registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yizhong; he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Gan, who held an honorary rank for longevity; his grandfather Cong was an Assistant Instructor, and his father Maozhong was a District Magistrate. His mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Liangbao and Liangbin, the latter a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his younger brothers were Liangcai, Liangshi, Liangchong, Liang'an, Liangjun, and Liangzhai. His wife was née Jiang. He placed fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yingqian, registered in a civilian household in Dongliu County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Diaoyuan; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Wei, who held an honorary rank for longevity; his grandfather was Zhen, and his father Wenjin. His mother was née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Yinglin, Yingding, Yingsheng, and Yingjin, and his wife was née Huang. He placed fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tang Yaoqin, registered in a military household in Changtai County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yinke; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuxu, his grandfather Yuangang, his father Ruxiang, and his mother née Yu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yaojian, Yaoluan, Yaoxuan, Yaoyue, and Xian [?]. His wife was née Liu. He ranked forty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Youci, registered in a military household of the Dezhou Left Guard in the Metropolitan Region and originally from Wendeng County, Shandong, was a student of the Dezhou school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Xiong, his father Jiapin, and his mother née Liu. His mother alone was living. His wife was née Liu. He ranked third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Zizhi, registered in a civilian household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and originally from Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shunju; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan. His grandfather Hao was a Medical Officer and received the honorary title of Prefectural Judge; his father Jie was Vice Commissioner of a Salt Distribution Commission. His father's former wife, née Shen, was posthumously granted the title of Lady for Attending, and his mother, née Wu, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zili, a physician authorized to wear official cap and girdle, and Zixuan. His wife was née Shen. He ranked fifty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xiao, registered in a military household in Zichuan County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yinliang; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen. His grandfather Kui received the honorary titles of Grand Master for Governance and Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father Chongyi was a Prefect. His father's former wife, née Xu, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability, and his mother, née Liu, was granted the same title. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Wu, Kuang, Du, Juan, Shu, Ye, and Shi. His wife was née Hu. He ranked thirty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.
