李丁〔貫山東兗州府曹州，民籍，州學增廣生，治《書經》，字明甫，行三，年三十，十二月十八日生〕。曾祖鳳，祖朴〔驛丞〕，父養性〔縣丞〕，母邵氏，繼母劉氏。具慶下，兄丙、寅，弟巳、庚，娶劉氏。山東鄉試第三十八名，會試第一百九十一名。

陳功〔貫山西太原府忻州，軍籍，州學生，治《書經》，字惟志，行二，年三十六，閏十二月十二日生〕。曾祖福，祖鸞，父大法〔壽官〕，母張氏。具慶下，弟勳、勔、勃，娶劉氏。山西鄉試第三名，會試第三百四十二名。

江文沛〔貫福建福州府閩縣，軍籍，縣學附學生，治《詩經》，字良雨，行四，年三十六，正月二十三日生〕。曾祖昌，祖元宦，父日德，母陳氏，繼母陳氏。慈侍下，弟文源、文深、文洲、文洙、文滙，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第二十六名，會試第三十一名。
translation_en:
Ge Dengming, registered in Biyang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daoxing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Sheng, his father Jie, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Yu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 318th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Ding, registered in Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student at the subprefectural government school, specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mingfu; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather Pu was a Postal Station Master; his father Yangxing was a County Vice Magistrate. His mother was née Shao, and his stepmother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bing and Yin, and his younger brothers Si and Geng. He married a woman née Liu. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Gong, registered in Xin Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Weizhi; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twelfth day of the intercalary twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Luan, and his father Dafa, who held an honorary official title for longevity. His mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xun, Mian, and Bo. He married a woman née Liu. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 342nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Wenpei, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an attached student at the county government school, specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Liangyu; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twenty-third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chang, his grandfather Yuanhuan, and his father Ride. His mother and stepmother were both née Chen. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Wenyuan, Wenshen, Wenzhou, Wenzhu, and Wenhui. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

龍宗武〔貫江西吉安府泰和縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字身之，行一，年二十九，七月初五日生〕。曾祖孔時，祖公寬，父天爵，嫡母嚴氏，生母王氏。永感下，兄孝卿、國卿，弟宗尚，娶尹氏。江西鄉試第六名，會試第一百九十名。

蕭彥〔貫直隸寧國府涇縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字思學，行三，年三十五，八月十六日生〕。曾祖士貴〔贈監察御史〕，祖瑞〔布政司右參議〕，父儲，母董氏。慈侍下，兄歆〔監生〕、豪，弟雍、韶、顏，娶趙氏。應天府鄉試第六十五名，會試第八名。
translation_en:
Li Xuan, a native of Taihe County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Weixian. He ranked second in his family and was twenty-five sui, born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather, Mao; and his father, Ziming, an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yu, and his younger brothers were Sui and Da. His wife was née Hua. He placed fourth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 339th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xiyuan, a native of Qishui County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was registered in a military household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Qishan. He ranked tenth in his family and was twenty-six sui, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hou; his grandfather, Zhongzheng, a District Magistrate; and his father, Chengfang. His father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Xizeng and Ximeng, both sacrificial officials (shengjiguan) [?], and Xicheng and Ximin; his younger brothers were Xiyong and Xizhu. His wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 351st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Long Zongwu, a native of Taihe County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a civilian household and was an added student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shenzhi. He ranked first in his family and was twenty-nine sui, born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kongshi; his grandfather, Gongkuan; and his father, Tianjue. His father's principal wife was née Yan, and his birth mother was née Wang. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xiaoqing and Guoqing, and his younger brother was Zongshang. His wife was née Yin. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Yan, a native of Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Sixue. He ranked third in his family and was thirty-five sui, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shigui, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather, Rui, was a Right Assistant Administration Commissioner; and his father was Chu. His mother was née Dong. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Xin, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Hao; his younger brothers were Yong, Shao, and Yan. His wife was née Zhao. He placed sixty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xie Shiqi 謝師啓, courtesy name Shumeng, was registered in a civilian household in Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-six sui, born on the thirtieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yunsheng, honorarily appointed Director in the Ministry of Rites; his grandfather was Cunru, Right Vice Minister of War; his father was Sanxun, an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Zheng. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shiyan, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year, Shiyan (師嚴), Shimian, Shizuo, and Shifan. His wife was née Jie. He placed tenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Shixin 葉時新, courtesy name Weihuai, was registered in a civilian household in Xiuning County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-four sui, born on the twentieth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yongfu, his grandfather Wulong, his father Xiu, and his mother née Cheng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shijie, and his younger brothers were Shijia, Shitai, Shiying, and Shikang. His wife was née Wu. He placed 128th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jian 陳薦, courtesy name Junyong, was registered in a civilian household in Qiyang County, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was twenty-seven sui, born on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhirong, his grandfather Xian, his father Liangneng, and his mother née Lei. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Su, Dian, and Ju, and his younger brother was Xuan. His wife was née Zhou. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Guanghao 周光鎬, courtesy name Guoyong, was registered in a civilian household in Chaoyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-two sui, born on the third day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Maoran, his grandfather Zhifang, his father Fuxian, a tribute scholar, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Guangde and Guangyang, both Imperial University students, Guangxun, and Guangming; his younger brother was Guangwei. His wife was née Zheng. He placed sixtieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Ting, registered in Pengxi County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yijin, he ranked first in family order, and he was thirty-five sui, born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhiguang; his grandfather, Pu, was a tribute student; his father was E; his father's principal wife was née He, and his birth mother was née Guo. His father was deceased and his mother was living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 362nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Zhengyi, registered in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shuming, he ranked twenty-fourth in family order, and he was thirty-two sui, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yantai, his grandfather Boxiang, his father Yangzhi, and his mother née Sun. His father was living and his mother was deceased. He married a woman née Wu. He placed seventy-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ruyu, registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Bowen, he ranked second in family order, and he was thirty-eight sui, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Gai, was a prefect; his grandfather, Yuanxun, was a provisioner (dianshan); his father, Yannian, was a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Rujin, and his younger brothers were Rujin (如錦), Ruyue, and Ru'ao. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 324th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Zongpan, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jianfu, he ranked second in family order, and he was twenty-eight sui, born on the fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Shizhe, held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Tianhuan, his father Xiang, and his mother née Zhu. His father was deceased and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Meng and Zongyue [?]; his younger brothers were Zongbi, a provincial graduate (juren), Zongfu, Zongqi, a student of the Directorate of Education, Zongjing, Zongxun, and Zongmo. He married a woman née Qiu. He placed sixty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Zizhang, courtesy name Xiangkui, was registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in birth order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongyu; his grandfather was Qishi, a government student granted the cap and girdle of official status; and his father was Yuanhong. His mother was née Xiao, and his stepmother née Luo. He had parents and a grandparent or grandparents living. His elder brothers were Ziheng and Zijing, and his younger brothers Xiangzhu and Ziyong. He married a woman née Xiao. He placed eighteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Daoqing, courtesy name Gongfu, was registered in a military household of Pingshan Guard, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Tianxi, and his father Jiang, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity. His mother was née Sun, and his stepmother née Xu. His father alone of his parents was living. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Tingcai, courtesy name Sijing, was registered in a military household in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked thirty-second in birth order and was thirty-eight years old, born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie, Vice Commissioner of a Salt Distribution Commission; his grandfather was Guangshou; and his father was Qi. His mother was née Xu, and his stepmothers were née Jiang and née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tingbin, and his younger brothers were Tingliang, Tingxie, Tingfeng, Tingzan, and Tingyi. He married a woman née Rao. He placed ninety-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dake, courtesy name Sijin, was registered in a civilian household in Tongzhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-four years old, born on the seventeenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chunde, posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master for Comprehensive Counsel and the offices of Right Vice Minister of Works and concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather was Chang, who received the same rank and offices through successive posthumous grants. His father was Yao, Left Vice Minister of Justice, and his mother was née Zhu, granted the title of Lady (shuren). He had parents and a grandparent or grandparents living. His elder brothers were Dazhen, an Imperial University student, and Dazhuang, a prefect; his younger brothers were Dayi, Daqian, Daqi, and Dasheng. He married a woman née Ling. He placed 131st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Yongxian 趙用賢, courtesy name Rushi, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was originally from Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the nineteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shi; his grandfather, Pin, was posthumously granted, through successive honors, the title of Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel; and his father, Chengqian, was Left Assistant Administration Commissioner. His father's principal wife, née Xiao, held the title Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother surviving. His elder brothers were Mao, Xian, and Yu [division of names uncertain]; his younger brothers were Yongbin, Yonggui, and Yongzhen. He married a woman née Zhang, then successively women née Tang and Chen. He placed eighty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Cheng 張程, courtesy name Yifu, was registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked fifty-seventh in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Fuhua, was Grand Master for Aid in Virtue, Senior Minister for Correct Governance, and Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; he was posthumously granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous name Jiansu. His grandfather, Wei, was granted the title Investigating Censor; his father, Aoshan, was Censor for the Supervision of Education. His father's former wife, née Ouyang, held the title Lady; his mother, née Zhou, held the title Grand Lady. His father was deceased and his mother surviving. His elder brothers were Zhi 祉, a National University student, and Zhi 秩, an Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy. He married a woman née Peng. He placed forty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Dai 錢岱, courtesy name Ruzhan, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Si, his grandfather Sheng, his father Heng, and his mother née Chu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dao, Ye, Yan, Yue, Xue, Luan, Jie, and E. He married a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Rulun 吳汝倫, courtesy name Wenxu, was registered in a military household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in his family and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zan, his grandfather Yingyuan, and his father Weixiao. His father's former wife was née Yang, his mother née Hua, and his stepmother also née Hua. His father was deceased and his mother surviving. His younger brother, Ruren, was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Shao and subsequently a woman née Cao. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Huaizhong, registered in Yiwu County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ruliang; he ranked sixth in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Keqing, his grandfather Xisheng, and his father Maoyuan; his mother was née Wu. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Chonghua, Huaiguang, and Huaide; his younger brothers were Chongxi, Chongzhen, Chongyin, Chongtai, Chongjie, Chonglie, Chongjia, Chongxiang, and Chongqi. He married a woman née Guo. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 390th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Bao, registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan, his grandfather Chen, and his father Yi; his mother was née Wang. His father alone survived. His elder brothers were Fu, Zuo [?], Ren, Jie, Yi, Ji, and Wei; his younger brothers were Jie and Yan. He married a woman née Jin. He placed forty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Dalun, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Renfu; he ranked eighteenth in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang, Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his grandfather was Yin, a Police Chief; his father was Zhi, and his mother was née Cen. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Dayuan and Dahua; his younger brothers were Damu, Datian, Dazuo, Dagui, Daqing, and Daxin. He married a woman née Xu, and subsequently women née Peng, Wang, and Fu. He placed thirty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Liangren, registered in Hanchuan County, Hanyang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhiyi; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dehong, his grandfather You (𧙗) [?], and his father Xun, a Sacrificial Officer; his mother was née Zhou. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Liangshi, an Usher, and his younger brother was Liangchun. He married a woman née Guo. He placed thirty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Jian 王緘, courtesy name Bomo, was registered in a civilian household in Wen’an County, Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Neng, was a county Registrar; his grandfather, Xian, was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor and subsequently granted the additional posthumous title of Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His father, Yi, was Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His father’s former wives were Lady Xing, posthumously granted the title Lady of Respect (gongren), and Lady Song, granted the title Lady for Courtesy (ruren); his mother, Lady Dong, was granted the title Lady of Respect. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Xu, Commander of the Hejian Guard; Wan, Ji, and Shen, all National University students; Shouxun, Cai, Zhi, Luo, Shan, Tong, and Zuan, a Prefect. His younger brothers were Lian, Si, and Yun. He married Lady Fan. He placed 104th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Bangyan [?] 黎邦琰 (Li Bangyan), courtesy name Junhua, was registered in a military household in Conghua County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather, Yuanchang, was granted the honorary title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather, Guan, served as Investigating Censor and was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Office of Imperial Seals. His father, Minbiao, was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his mother was Lady Liang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bangjiu, Bangli, Bangxian, Bangqiu, Banglu, Banglin, Bangtian, Banggong, and Bangqi [?] 邦𤪌. He married Lady Chen. He placed twenty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Shichu 曾士楚, courtesy name Ziqiao, was registered in Conghua County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a native of Panyu County. An additional student of the Conghua County school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in birth order and was forty years old, born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather was Guanhou; and his father, Chuo, was a School Instructor. His mother was Lady Zhang and his stepmother Lady Zhong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shouqian and Shoumo; his younger brothers were Shimao, Shilin, Shisen, Shijun, Shihong, Shiqian, Shishi [?] 士𣐈, Shibiao, and Shicheng. He married Lady Yu. He placed fifty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei Jiaxiang 雷嘉祥, courtesy name Heqing, was registered in a military household in Jingyan County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the thirtieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Tianjian; his grandfather was Shoucheng; his father was Ming; and his mother was Lady Wu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Jiatai. He married Lady Li. He placed fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

===
李忱貫福建泉州府晉江縣民籍　縣學生
治易經字誠甫行四年三十七月初四日生
曾祖瑄〔七品散官〕
祖孚　父士夔　母丁氏　繼母陳氏
永感下　兄材　大洵　大進　弟大瀾〔知州〕大灝　大潞　大漂　大涔　大淮　大清　娶張氏
福建鄉試第十一名　會試第二十三名
林庭植貫福建福州府福清縣軍籍　府學生
治詩經字槐卿行五年三十二十月十七日生
曾祖元
祖慶　父晚翠　母謝氏
慈侍下　兄庭材　弟養盛　養辦　養晦　養端　養初　養蒙　養潛　養氣　養高　娶余氏
福建鄉試第十六名　會試第二百九名
punctuated:
雙鳳鳴〔貫陝西慶陽衛軍籍，山西文水縣人，慶陽府學生，治詩經，字維禎，行一，年三十五，二月十四日生〕。曾祖英，祖鉞，父臣〔冠帶生員〕，母王氏，繼母孫氏、黃氏。具慶下，娶樊氏。陝西鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百二十四名。

胡宥〔貫直隸徽州府休寧縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字子仁，行四，年三十一，四月二十七日生〕。曾祖仕茂，祖永華，父正禎，嫡母程氏，生母毛氏。慈侍下，兄寵、寬、宇，弟寀、賓、宣，娶方氏，繼娶黃氏。應天府鄉試第七名，會試第二百九十二名。

李忱〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字誠甫，行四，年三十，七月初四日生〕。曾祖瑄〔七品散官〕，祖至，父士夔，母丁氏，繼母陳氏。永感下，兄世材、大洵、大進，弟大瀾〔知州〕、大灝、大潞、大潔、大浡、大淮、大清，娶張氏。福建鄉試第十一名，會試第二十三名。

林庭植〔貫福建福州府福清縣軍籍，府學生，治詩經，字槐卿，行五，年三十二，十月十七日生〕。曾祖元，祖慶，父晚翠，母謝氏。慈侍下，兄庭材，弟養盛、養翀、養聯、養端、養初、養蒙、養潛、養氣、養高，娶余氏。福建鄉試第十六名，會試第二百九名。
translation_en:
Shuang Fengming, courtesy name Weizhen, was registered in a military household of Qingyang Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Wenshui County, Shanxi. A student of the Qingyang Prefectural School specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the fourteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Yue; and his father, Chen, a government student granted the cap and girdle of official status. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmothers were née Sun and née Huang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Fan. He placed forty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu You, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in a civilian household of Xiuning County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An additional-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shimao; his grandfather, Yonghua; and his father, Zhengzhen. His father's principal wife was née Cheng, and his birth mother was née Mao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Chong, Kuan, and Yu; his younger brothers were Cai, Bin, and Xuan. His wife was née Fang; he subsequently married a woman née Huang. He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chen, courtesy name Chengfu, was registered in a civilian household of Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, a prestige official of the seventh rank; his grandfather, Zhi; and his father, Shikui. His mother was née Ding, and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shicai, Daxun, and Dajin; his younger brothers were Dalan, a department magistrate, Dahao, Dalu, Dajie, Dabo, Dah uai, and Daqing. His wife was née Zhang. He placed eleventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Tingzhi, courtesy name Huaiqing, was registered in a military household of Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather, Qing; and his father, Wancui. His mother was née Xie. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Tingcai; his younger brothers were Yangsheng, Yangchong, Yanglian, Yangduan, Yangchu, Yangmeng, Yangqian, Yangqi, and Yanggao. His wife was née Yu. He placed sixteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
沈涵〔貫武功左衛匠籍，浙江德清縣人，國子生，治詩經，字維敬，行一，年三十一，六月二十四日生〕。曾祖銓，祖謐，父珏〔兵部主事〕，母王氏。慈侍下，弟濳，娶吳氏。順天府鄉試第七十六名，會試第一百三十四名。

莊鵬舉〔貫直隸河間府景州東光縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字圖南，行一，年三十五，八月二十七日生〕。曾祖欽，祖鐸，父敬〔貢士〕，母劉氏。永感下，弟鵬程，娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第四十八名，會試第二百八十三名。

張第〔貫山東東昌府茌平縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝登，行一，年三十四，二月十二日生〕。曾祖寬，祖榮，父經〔省祭官〕，嫡母邵氏，生母孟氏。慈侍下，兄魯〔陰陽訓術〕、簪、範、笙，弟筠、籌，娶劉氏。山東鄉試第五十名，會試第三百三十六名。

丁賓〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉善縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字禮原，行三，年二十九，正月初一日生〕。曾祖弼，祖乾，父衮〔典儀〕，母呂氏，繼母陸氏。重慶下，兄寅〔監生〕，娶吳氏。順天府鄉試第五十五名，會試第三百九十一名。
translation_en:
Shen Han, courtesy name Weijing, was registered in an artisan household of the Wugong Left Guard and was a native of Deqing County, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan, his grandfather Mi, and his father Jue, a Secretary in the Ministry of War; his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother was Qian, and his wife was née Wu. He placed seventy-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhuang Pengju, courtesy name Tunan, was registered in a civilian household in Dongguang County, Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Rites. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin, his grandfather Duo, and his father Jing, a tribute scholar; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Pengcheng, and his wife was née Liu. He placed forty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Di, courtesy name Rudeng, was registered in a military household in Chiping County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twelfth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kuan, his grandfather Rong, and his father Jing, a Sacrificial Attendant. His father's principal wife was née Shao, and his birth mother was née Meng. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Lu, an Instructor in the Yin-yang School, Zan, Fan, and Sheng; his younger brothers were Yun and Chou. His wife was née Liu. He placed fiftieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and three hundred thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Bin, courtesy name Liyuan, was registered in a military household in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bi, his grandfather Qian, and his father Gun, a Ceremonial Officer; his mother was née Lü, and his stepmother was née Lu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother Yin was a student of the Directorate of Education, and his wife was née Wu. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 隆慶五年進士登科錄

賀南儒〔貫浙江嘉興府海鹽縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治禮記，字懷珍，行一，年三十一，十二月十七日生〕。曾祖宥，祖岳，父陛〔縣丞〕，母朱氏，繼母鞏氏。具慶下，弟南良、南征、南極、南閩，娶陸氏。浙江鄉試第七十二名，會試第二百一名。

鄭時章〔貫福建漳州府龍溪縣，軍籍，縣學生，治禮記，字文敘，行二，年三十二，五月初八日生〕。曾祖凱中，祖顯進，父重享，母陳氏。永感下，兄時可，弟雲騰，娶許氏。福建鄉試第五十八名，會試第二百六十七名。

林應訓〔貫福建福州府懷安縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字子啓，行三，年三十六，七月十六日生〕。曾祖寳，祖黙，父世靈〔巡檢〕，母葉氏。永感下，兄應詔、應試，弟應誥，娶張氏。福建鄉試第七名，會試第一百二十名。

田琯〔貫福建延平府大田縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字希玉，行四，年三十二，十一月十七日生〕。曾祖賜祿〔壽官〕，祖廣榮，父鈇，母陳氏。慈侍下，兄頊〔按察司提學副使〕、華、洙〔武學訓導〕、瑚，弟圭，娶林氏。順天府鄉試第六十四名，會試第八十三名。
translation_en:
He Nanru, of Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Huaizhen. He ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one sui, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was You, his grandfather Yue, and his father Bi, a County Vice Magistrate. His mother was née Zhu, and his stepmother née Gong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Nanliang, Nanzheng, Nanji, and Nanmin. He married a woman née Lu. He placed seventy-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Shizhang, of Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a county-school student. He specialized in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Wenxu. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-two sui, born on the eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Kaizhong, his grandfather Xianjin, and his father Zhongxiang; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Shike, and his younger brother Yunteng. He married a woman née Xu. He placed fifty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yingxun, of Huai'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county-school student. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziqi. He ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-six sui, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Bao, his grandfather Mo, and his father Shiling, a Police Chief; his mother was née Ye. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yingzhao and Yingshi, and his younger brother Yinggao. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Guan, of Datian County, Yanping Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Xiyu. He ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-two sui, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Cilu, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather was Guangrong, and his father Fu. His mother was née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Xu, an Education Intendant serving as Vice Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission; Hua; Zhu, an Assistant Instructor at a military school; and Hu. His younger brother was Gui. He married a woman née Lin. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 隆慶五年進士登科錄
text:
陳贊〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣軍籍國子生治詩經字宗謨行七年三十九五月二十六日生〕
曾祖聰〔縣主簿贈監察御史〕祖奎〔布政司左布政使〕父冠〔工部郎中加正四品服俸〕嫡母張氏〔封宜人〕生母張氏
永感下兄贇贄〔監生〕貞〔監生〕弟賡娶胡氏

translation_en:
Chen Zan, registered in a military household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zongmo; he ranked seventh in his family and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Cong was a County Registrar, posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his grandfather Kui was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his father Guan was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works, granted the dress and salary of the principal fourth rank. His father's principal wife, née Zhang, was invested as Lady of Suitability; his birth mother was also née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yun, Zhi (a National University student), and Zhen (a National University student); his younger brother was Geng. He married a woman née Hu. He placed fifty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yiwei, registered in a military household in Qishui County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zonglu; he ranked seventh in his family and was twenty-six years old, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Shaoli was a Keeper of Seals; his grandfather was Ban, his father Wenyan, and his mother née Yao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yiyue and Yiqu. He married a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhen was registered in an official household in Qingyang Guard, Shaanxi, and was originally from Datong Guard, Shanxi. He was a student of the Anhua County school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Weiqing; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Ze and grandfather Xian were both Guard Commanders; his father was Chaochun and his mother née Sun. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Dong and Ying. He married a woman née Yang. He placed sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yu, registered in a civilian household in Guo County, Dai Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the county school specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Fan was a County Magistrate; his grandfather Zhi was an annual tribute student; his father was Jiyuan and his mother née Guo. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Zhong, Shu, and Nian; his younger brothers were Ci, Cong, Yi, Xi, Ken, and Yuan. He married a woman née Wang. He placed ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 331st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Changzu 陳長祚, courtesy name Yijie, was registered in a military household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A supplementary student of the county school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. He ranked first in birth order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Ci and grandfather Dalun were both posthumously appointed Investigating Censors. His father Rui was a Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; his mother, née Lin, held the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Changtai, Changyun, Changjin, Changdao, Changshen, and Changming; his younger brothers were Changfa, Changsheng, Changgeng, Changmian, Changmei, Changze, Changchao, and Changqing. His wife was née Li. He placed fortieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Yingqi 袁應旂, courtesy name Bangshi, was registered in a military household in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. An added student of the county school, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. He ranked sixth in birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the tenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Xizhi had been granted the right to wear an official cap and belt under applicable regulations; his grandfather was Shili, and his father was Yu. His mother, née Wu, was living, and his father was deceased. His younger brothers were Yingjing, Yingfu, Yinglu, and Yingchang. His wife was née Zou. He placed sixteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shicheng 李時成, courtesy name Weizhong, was registered in a civilian household in Qishui County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. He ranked second in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yongqi, his grandfather was Xian, and his father was Tingzhi; his mother was née Yue. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shucheng; his younger brothers were Weicheng, Ancheng, Wancheng, Xiaocheng, Xuancheng, and Yingcheng. His wife was née Wu. He placed twenty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shangzhi 劉尚志, courtesy name Ruli, was registered in a civilian household in Huaining County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Qianshan County. A student of the Huaining county school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. He ranked second in birth order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the nineteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Daoxu, his grandfather was Kai, and his father was Zhao; his mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shangren (annotation unclear: 洋省祭 [?]) and Shangjue; his younger brothers were Shangzhong, Shangxin, and Shangyou. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張學道〔貫陝西西安府盩厔縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字子愛，行三，年三十一，九月二十一日生〕。曾祖麟〔贈工部主事〕，祖玘〔布政司左參政〕，父幾〔按察司僉事〕，母王氏〔封宜人〕。嚴侍下，兄學詩〔知縣〕、學禮〔知縣〕，弟學行、學書，娶王氏，繼娶吳氏。陝西鄉試第四十名，會試第三百三十二名。

劉應元〔貫山西平陽府洪洞縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字子春，行四，年三十六，二月十六日生〕。曾祖恭〔封文林郎、兵馬副指揮〕，祖榮〔通判，贈奉直大夫、知州〕，父廷臣〔都察院右副都御史〕，母段氏〔贈宜人〕，繼母段氏〔封宜人〕。永感下，兄應時〔按察司副使〕、應科〔貢士〕、應才〔監生〕，弟應魁、應熊、應龍、應舉、應制、應詔、應和，娶衛氏。山西鄉試第十三名，會試第二百四十七名。

顧其志〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字太冲，行一，年二十六，七月初八日生〕。曾祖顯，祖鉞，父汝玉，母王氏，繼母莊氏。重慶下，弟其悳、其愈，娶丘氏。應天府鄉試第十九名，會試第一百六十三名。
translation_en:
Li Shi, courtesy name Ruoxu, was registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Sichuan. An additional student of the subprefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongsheng, an annual tribute student; his grandfather was Ao, a Magistrate posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father was Weikang, and his mother was née Min. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Men, Jiao, Ge, Chi, and Xiang, and his younger brothers were Can, Wan, Yu, Xuan, Shu, Chen, Ning, Huan, and Cha (the transcription and division of these names are uncertain [?]). His wife was née Yan. He placed fifty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 384th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xuedao, courtesy name Ziai, was registered in a civilian household in Zhouzhi County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. An additional student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, posthumously granted the title of Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather was Qi, Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his father was Ji, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in a Provincial Surveillance Commission; and his mother was née Wang, granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Xueshi and Xueli, both Magistrates, and his younger brothers were Xuexing and Xueshu. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed fortieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 332nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yingyuan, courtesy name Zichun, was registered in a military household in Hongdong County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked fourth in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gong, granted the titles of Gentleman for Cultivated Service and Vice Commander of a Wardens’ Office; his grandfather was Rong, an Assistant Prefect posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Upright Service and Subprefect; his father was Tingchen, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate; his mother was née Duan, posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability; and his stepmother was also née Duan, granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yingshi, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Surveillance Commission; Yingke, a tribute scholar; and Yingcai, a student of the Directorate of Education. His younger brothers were Yingkui, Yingxiong, Yinglong, Yingju, Yingzhi, Yingzhao, and Yinghe. His wife was née Wei. He placed thirteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Qizhi, courtesy name Taichong, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-six, born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Yue, and his father Ruyu; his mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Zhuang. Grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Qide and Qiyu, and his wife was née Qiu. He placed nineteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

費標〔貫順天府大興縣，冨戶籍，浙江慈谿縣人，國子生，治詩經，字孟立，行一，年四十八，八月初四日生。〕曾祖燦〔通判，贈大理寺右寺丞〕，祖鎧〔大理寺左寺丞〕，父沐〔通判〕，前母劉氏〔贈安人〕，母王氏〔封安人〕。永感下，弟桐〔府知事〕、桂〔知縣〕。娶張氏，繼娶許氏。順天府鄉試第一百名，會試第一百八十九名。

阮尚賓〔貫雲南大理府太和縣，民籍，府學增廣生，治易經，字君重，行一，年三十九，九月初二日生。〕曾祖俊，祖宏，父應文〔壽官〕，母王氏。慈侍下，弟尚賢、尚友。娶李氏。雲南鄉試第二十名，會試第一百二名。

許一德〔貫貴州貴州衛，官籍，直隸泗州人，國子生，治易經，字子恒，行三，年三十二，九月十八日生。〕曾祖宣〔指揮僉事〕，祖祿〔指揮僉事〕，父奇〔府同知〕，前母胡氏，母易氏。具慶下，兄脩德〔正千戶〕、懋德，弟育德、崇德〔貢士〕、裕德〔貢士〕、厚德、成德。娶越氏。貴州鄉試第一名，會試第三百十七名。

王許之〔貫江西瑞州府高安縣，民籍，府學生，治易經，字以忠，行九，年二十八，十一月十八日生。〕曾祖舜韶，祖禹都，父湯相，母尚氏，繼母况氏。具慶下，弟訓之、誦之、誥之。娶朱氏。江西鄉試第七十五名，會試第五十四名。
translation_en:
Fei Biao, courtesy name Mengli, was registered in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, in the wealthy-household category; his ancestral home was Cixi County, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged forty-eight, and born on the fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Can, was an assistant prefect, posthumously appointed Right Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review; his grandfather, Kai, was Left Assistant Director of that court; and his father, Mu, was an assistant prefect. His father's former wife, née Liu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace; his mother, née Wang, was granted the same title. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Tong, a prefectural clerk, and Gui, a county magistrate. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed one hundredth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ruan Shangbin, courtesy name Junzhong, was registered as a civilian in Taihe County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather was Hong; his father, Yingwen, held an honorary official title granted for longevity; and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Shangxian and Shangyou. He married a woman née Li. He placed twentieth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and one hundred second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yide, courtesy name Ziheng, was registered in the officer-household category in Guizhou Guard, Guizhou; his ancestral home was Sizhou in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Xuan, and grandfather, Lu, were both assistant commanders; his father, Qi, was a prefectural vice prefect. His father's former wife was née Hu, and his mother was née Yi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiude, a battalion commander, and Maode; his younger brothers were Yude 育德, Chongde and Yude 裕德, both Metropolitan Examination graduates awaiting the Palace Examination, Houde, and Chengde. He married a woman née Yue. He placed first in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and three hundred seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuzhi, courtesy name Yizhong, was registered as a civilian in Gao'an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was ninth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shunshao; his grandfather was Yudu; his father was Tangxiang; his mother was née Shang; and his stepmother was née Kuang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xunzhi, Songzhi, and Gaozhi. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed seventy-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

孫繼先〔貫山西太原府盂縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字胤甫，行二，年三十二，二月二十一日生〕。曾祖文顯，祖愷，父希哲，母張氏。具慶下，兄繼芳，弟繼原，娶張氏。山西鄉試第二十七名，會試第三百三十八名。

謝師彦〔貫湖廣武昌府蒲圻縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字叔美，行二，年二十三，三月二十五日生〕。曾祖允勝〔封禮部郎中〕，祖存儒〔兵部右侍郎〕，父三訓〔監生〕，母鄭氏。重慶下，兄師啟〔同科進士〕，弟師嚴、師勉、師作、師範，娶金氏。湖廣鄉試第三十七名，會試第一百名。

喬巖〔貫河南歸德府商丘縣民籍，府學生，治易經，字巽甫，行二，年三十四，三月初七日生〕。曾祖福，祖志賢，父舉，嫡母朱氏，生母張氏。永感下，兄嶽，弟嵩、崑、嵐、岏，娶萬氏。河南鄉試第六十名，會試第一百六十八名。

齊世臣〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字惟良，行一，年三十一，九月初七日生〕。曾祖魯，祖海，父遂，母姚氏。慈侍下，弟世美、世望、世用、世際、世冑、世守、世華、世德、世和，娶喻氏。江西鄉試第六十四名，會試第二百五十四名。
translation_en:
Sun Jixian, registered in a civilian household in Yu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yinfu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenxian, his grandfather Kai, his father Xizhe, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jifang and his younger brother Jiyuan; he married a woman née Zhang. He ranked twenty-seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 338th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Shiyan, registered in a civilian household in Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shumei; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunsheng, granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Rites; his grandfather was Cunru, Right Vice Minister of War; his father was Sanxun, an Imperial Academy student; and his mother was née Zheng. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Shiqi, a metropolitan graduate of the same examination year; his younger brothers were Shiyan 師嚴, Shimian, Shizuo, and Shifan. He married a woman née Jin. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiao Yan, registered in a civilian household in Shangqiu County, Guide Prefecture, Henan, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xunfu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Zhixian, and his father Ju; his father's principal wife was née Zhu and his birth mother née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yue, and his younger brothers were Song, Kun, Lan, and Wan. He married a woman née Wan. He ranked sixtieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Shichen, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weiliang; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu, his grandfather Hai, his father Sui, and his mother née Yao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Shimei, Shiwang, Shiyong, Shiji 世際, Shizhou, Shishou, Shihua, Shide, and Shihe. He married a woman née Yu. He ranked sixty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 隆慶五年進士登科錄
text:
伍士望〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣匠籍府學生治詩經字景周行三年三十七十二月二十七日生〕
曾祖復祖良父守中〔庫大使〕母董氏
慈侍下娶鍾氏

translation_en:
Wu Shiwang, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jingzhou, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was aged thirty-seven and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather, Liang; and his father, Shouzhong, a Storehouse Commissioner. His mother was née Dong. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His wife was née Zhong. He placed thirty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Ru, registered in Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Zicheng, and he ranked fourth among his brothers. He was aged thirty-seven and was born on the nineteenth day of the intercalary sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Gan, who held honorary official rank for longevity; and his father, Yue, a tribute student. His legal mother was née Jia, and his birth mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Qian, a School Instructor; Jin, a District Magistrate; Zhi; and Fa. His wife was née Shang. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 395th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yixun, registered in Ningyang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Tianxu, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was aged thirty-four and was born on the tenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather, Xun; his father, Zi; and his mother, née Song. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Shu, a Sacrificial Attendant; his younger brothers were Yiqi, Yijiao, Yixing, and Yixian. His wife was née Wan. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang De, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to an artisan household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Benming, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was aged thirty-four and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Gao; and his father, Shihe. His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother was née Huang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were En and Shu; his younger brothers were Ci and Cong. His wife was née Wu. He placed forty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 340th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
蘇湖〔貫雲南大理府太和縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字望涯，行一，年三十三，七月二十五日生〕。曾祖胤瑄，祖銳，父鵬程，母李氏。具慶下，兄愚〔衛經歷〕、淮、偉〔知縣〕、江，弟浙、沂，娶李氏。雲南鄉試第十名，會試第三百十二名。

translation_en:
Su Hu, registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wangya; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yinxuan, his grandfather Rui, and his father Pengcheng; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yu (a Guard Command registrar), Huai, Wei (a county magistrate), and Jiang; his younger brothers were Zhe and Yi. His wife was née Li. He placed tenth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Kezheng, registered in a civilian household in Conghua County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Maoyi; he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yan, his grandfather Yingke (a tribute scholar), and his father Ge (a county magistrate); his mother was née Ouyang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Meng. He placed seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Jieyong, registered in a civilian household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yizhen; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Shanggong, his grandfather Jinding, and his father Di; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shenyong, Liyong, Renyong, Shiyong, Wangyong, Zhiyong, Jiyong, Fuyong, Jingyong, Sheyong, and Dayong. His wife was née Peng. He placed fourteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 360th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Pengfei, registered in a civilian household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student of the prefectural government school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xihan; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hongmei, his grandfather Qiaomu, and his father Jingxie; his mother was née Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiteng, Changchun, Huichun, and Qin; his younger brothers were Shuchun, Yi, Xu, Yan, and Huan. His wife was née Zeng. He placed forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

邢玠〔貫山東青州府益都縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字搢伯，行一，年三十二，九月二十七日生〕。曾祖端，祖聰，父鑌，母鄭氏。慈侍下，娶王氏。山東鄉試第四十四名，會試第一百十五名。

translation_en:
Yu Ruwei, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yuanxuan, and he ranked first in birth order. He was twenty-eight, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Lin, a prefectural judge; his grandfather was Xu; and his father was Mingshi, a tribute scholar (gongshi). His mother was née Song, and his stepmothers were née Yang, Li, and Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ruxie and Ruyi, and his younger brothers were Ruji, Rumei, and Rulin. He married a woman née Zhuang and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Yang. He placed forty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Weicheng, registered in Qiu County, Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zongfu, and he ranked first in birth order. He was thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was You, his grandfather was Qi, his father was Shangxian, and his mother was née Jing. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently married a woman née Li. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xing Jie, registered in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Jinbo, and he ranked first in birth order. He was thirty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather was Cong, his father was Bin, and his mother was née Zheng. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhiju, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Mingyu, and he ranked first in birth order. He was thirty-three, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Yan and grandfather Jian both held honorary official titles awarded for longevity; his father was Yao, and his mother was née Lin. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brother Zhishu was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Huang. He placed sixty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

text:

重慶下弟起元體元娶范氏
應天府鄉試第二十二名會試第一百三十三名
張維翰〔貫山東東昌府茌平縣軍籍縣學生治詩經字邦楨行一年三十三月二十五日生〕
曾祖訪祖文祥〔知縣〕父後奇〔巡檢〕前母姜氏母靖氏繼母劉氏
具慶下兄一本四教五典紹芝弟弘訓維垣紹芳娶楊氏

===

貫直隸安慶府潛山縣軍籍　國子生

曾祖道〔通判〕　祖峘　父瀅〔知府 同〕　前母儲氏　母丁氏

高自治
貫山西太原右衛官籍　國子生
治禮記字思勉行一年三十四月十八日生
曾祖謙〔壽官〕　祖泰　父典　母張氏　繼母馬氏李氏
具慶下　弟自強　自學　自立　自明　自新　娶蕭氏
順天府鄉試第四十八名　會試第二百三十四名
punctuated:
唐應元〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字子春，行一，年二十八，九月初一日生〕。曾祖澄，祖昊，父鳳翔，母孫氏，繼母嚴氏。重慶下，弟起元、體元，娶范氏。應天府鄉試第二十二名，會試第一百三十三名。

張維翰〔貫山東東昌府茌平縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字邦楨，行一，年三十，三月二十五日生〕。曾祖訪，祖文祥〔知縣〕，父後奇〔巡檢〕，前母姜氏，母靖氏，繼母劉氏。具慶下，兄一本、四教、五典、紹芝，弟弘訓、維垣、紹芳，娶楊氏。山東鄉試第五十名，會試第三百二十三名。

王嘉柔〔貫直隸安慶府潛山縣，軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字惟則，行二，年三十三，九月初四日生〕。曾祖道〔通判〕，祖峘，父堂〔府同知〕，前母儲氏，母丁氏。永感下，兄嘉桀，弟嘉檠、嘉寀，娶韓氏。應天府鄉試第四十六名，會試第二百七十名。

高自治〔貫山西太原右衛，官籍，國子生，治禮記，字思勉，行一，年三十，四月十八日生〕。曾祖謙〔壽官〕，祖泰，父雲，母張氏，繼母馬氏、李氏。具慶下，弟自強、自學、自立、自明、自新，娶蕭氏。順天府鄉試第四十八名，會試第二百三十四名。
translation_en:
Tang Yingyuan, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zichun; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Hao, and his father Fengxiang; his mother was née Sun and his stepmother née Yan. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Qiyuan and Tiyuan, and his wife was née Fan. He placed twenty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Weihan, registered in Chiping County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bangzhen; he ranked first in his family and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Fang; his grandfather Wenxiang was a magistrate, and his father Houqi was a police chief. His father's former wife was née Jiang, his mother née Jing, and his stepmother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yiben, Sijiao, Wudian, and Shaozhi; his younger brothers were Hongxun, Weiyuan, and Shaofang. His wife was née Yang. He placed fiftieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 323rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiarou, registered in Qianshan County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Weize; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-three years old, born on the fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Dao was an assistant prefect; his grandfather was Huan, and his father Tang was a vice prefect. His father's former wife was née Chu, and his mother was née Ding. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jiajie, and his younger brothers were Jiaqing and Jiacai. His wife was née Han. He placed forty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Zizhi, registered in the Taiyuan Right Guard, Shanxi, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Simian; he ranked first in his family and was thirty years old, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather Qian held an honorary rank for longevity; his grandfather was Tai, and his father Yun. His mother was née Zhang, and his successive stepmothers were née Ma and née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ziqiang, Zixue, Zili, Ziming, and Zixin. His wife was née Xiao. He placed forty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

孫訓〔貫山西太原右衛官籍，直隸高郵州人，太原府學生，治詩經，字廷揚，行二，年二十八，三月二十七日生〕。曾祖景，祖憲〔累封奉直大夫、尚寶司少卿〕，父允中〔應天府府丞〕，母張氏〔贈宜人〕，繼母李氏、尋氏〔封宜人〕。嚴侍下，兄鑰、謨〔指揮僉事〕，弟誥〔武舉〕、詔、諒、讚，娶潘氏。山西鄉試第十九名，會試第二百十九名。

陳用賓〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣軍籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字道亨，行二，年二十八，二月初十日生〕。曾祖惠，祖遜，父春，前母林氏，母許氏。慈侍下，兄文偉、奇偉，弟用宏、用寅、用實，娶趙氏。福建鄉試第七十名，會試第二百二十六名。

金從洋〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣民籍，上海縣人，華亭縣學附學生，治詩經，字汝孝，行一，年三十一，正月初五日生〕。曾祖顯，祖廷璋，父鍾，母管氏。慈侍下，弟自洋、繼洋、祖洋、煥洋，娶汪氏。應天府鄉試第十一名，會試第二百八十四名。

汪彥冲〔貫直隸徽州府歙縣民籍，浙江仁和縣人，國子生，治詩經，字懋中，行一，年二十九，二月十六日生〕。曾祖社貞，祖尚，父世明，母姚氏。具慶下，兄彥衡，娶葉氏。順天府鄉試第二名，會試第二百二十九名。
translation_en:
Sun Xun, courtesy name Tingyang, was registered in an official household of the Taiyuan Right Guard, Shanxi, and was a native of Gaoyou Subprefecture in the Metropolitan Region. A student of the Taiyuan Prefectural School, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked second in birth order, was twenty-eight sui, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Xian, received successive honorary grants as Grand Master for Upright Service and Vice Director of the Office of Imperial Seals. His father, Yunzhong, was Assistant Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture. His mother, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmothers were née Li and née Xun, with the latter recorded as having been granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Yue and Mo, the latter an Assistant Commander; his younger brothers were Gao, a military provincial graduate, Zhao, Liang, and Zan. He married a woman née Pan. He placed nineteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Yongbin, courtesy name Daoheng, was registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the county school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked second in birth order, was twenty-eight sui, and was born on the tenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui, his grandfather Xun, and his father Chun. His father's former wife was née Lin, and his mother was née Xu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Wenwei and Qiwei; his younger brothers were Yonghong, Yongyin, and Yongshi. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed seventieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Congyang, courtesy name Ruxiao, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, and was a native of Shanghai County. An additional student of the Huating County School, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first in birth order, was thirty-one sui, and was born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Tingzhang, his father Zhong, and his mother née Guan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Ziyang, Jiyang, Zuyang, and Huanyang. He married a woman née Wang. He placed eleventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yanchong, courtesy name Maozhong, was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, and was a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first in birth order, was twenty-nine sui, and was born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shezhen, his grandfather Shang, his father Shiming, and his mother née Yao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yanheng. He married a woman née Ye. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳琯〔貫福建漳州府漳浦縣民籍，府學增廣生，治詩經，字邦燮，行九，年二十七，閏正月三十日生〕。曾祖震〔市舶司副提舉〕，祖涵〔七品散官〕，父師旦，母許氏。具慶下，兄瑛〔貢士〕、璦、珂、璉、玠、珙、珍、璿、琚、璁，弟珀、瑚、球、珣、瑄、琉、瑢、璞，娶許氏。福建鄉試第八十五名，會試第二百六名。

王延〔貫四川順慶府南充縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字子長，行二，年四十一，十一月十一日生〕。曾祖昺〔壽官〕，祖銳〔贈通議大夫、戶部左侍郎，加贈資政大夫、都察院左都御史〕，父希文〔封戶部主事，累贈資政大夫、都察院左都御史〕，母馬氏〔封安人，累贈夫人〕。永感下，兄廷〔資德大夫、正治上卿、都察院左都御史〕，娶張氏。四川鄉試第二十七名，會試第二百三十七名。

俞文達〔貫直隸徽州府婺源縣軍籍，府學生，治書經，字行之，行一，年三十五，三月初十日生〕。曾祖宗哲，祖尹僖，父燦榮，母汪氏。慈侍下，弟文道〔貢士〕，娶汪氏，繼娶方氏。應天府鄉試第一百四十七名，會試第一百十六名。
translation_en:
Fan Mingqian 范鳴謙, registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhenfu; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Weishan, his grandfather Bingdao, his father Mu, and his mother née Bian. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Minghe, and his wife was née Xu. He placed 125th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 344th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Guan 吳琯, registered in a civilian household in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the prefectural Confucian school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bangxie; he ranked ninth in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirtieth day of the intercalary first month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, Vice Superintendent of the Maritime Trade Superintendency; his grandfather was Han, a holder of a seventh-rank prestige title; his father was Shidan; and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ying, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Ai, Ke, Lian, Jie, Gong, Zhen, Xuan, Ju, and Cong; his younger brothers were Po, Hu, Qiu, Xun, Xuan, Liu, Rong, and Pu. His wife was née Xu. He placed eighty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yan 王延, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zichang; he ranked second in his family and was aged forty-one, born on the eleventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Bing, an honorary official by virtue of longevity. His grandfather Rui was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Revenue, and additionally Grand Master for Governance Assistance and Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father Xiwen was granted the title Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and, through successive posthumous grants, Grand Master for Governance Assistance and Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Ma, was granted the title Lady of Peace and, through successive posthumous grants, Lady. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Ting held the titles Grand Master for Moral Assistance and Senior Minister for True Governance and served as Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Wenda 俞文達, registered in a military household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the prefectural Confucian school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xingzhi; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the tenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zongzhe, his grandfather Yinxi, his father Canrong, and his mother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother Wendao was a tribute scholar (gongshi). His wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was née Fang. He placed 147th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

黃克念〔貫河南歸德府寧陵縣軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字睿卿，行一，年二十六，十二月二十九日生〕。曾祖綬，祖榜，父卷〔貢士〕，母王氏。具慶下，弟克嶷、克壯、克家，娶張氏，繼娶李氏。河南鄉試第二十六名，會試第二百八十八名。
translation_en:
Wang Ruxun, registered in a military household in Liaocheng County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was an additional student at the county school and specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shigu; he ranked first in birth order, was twenty-one years old, and was born on the nineteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao, his grandfather Kui, and his father Fan; his father's principal wife was Lady Liu, and his birth mother was Lady Zeng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ruqian, and his younger brothers were Rujin and Ruyong. He married Lady Tian. He placed nineteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Mou, registered in an officer household of the Sizhou Guard, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he ranked first in birth order, was thirty years old, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhen, grandfather Qing, and father Tang each served as a Company Commander. His father's principal wife was Lady Hu, and his birth mother was Lady Xu. Both parents were deceased. He placed sixty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Mengxiong, registered in a civilian household in Nanling County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, was a county school student and specialized in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Yingnan; he ranked eighth in birth order, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Yun served as a District Magistrate, and his father Chengke served as a County Registrar. His mother was Lady Zhu, and his stepmother was Lady Hu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Menggui and Menglou; his younger brothers were Menglong, Mengpi, Mengfu, Mengyuan, and Mengqi. He married Lady Tao. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Kenian, registered in a military household in Ningling County, Guide Prefecture, Henan, was a county school student and specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruiqing; he ranked first in birth order, was twenty-six years old, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shou, his grandfather Bang, and his father Juan, a tribute scholar; his mother was Lady Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Keyi, Kezhuang, and Kejia. He married Lady Zhang and subsequently Lady Li. He placed twenty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.
