translation_en:
Qi Jing, registered in a civilian household in Fucheng County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zihua; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao; his grandfather, Jie, served as an unranked functionary; his father was Xian, and his mother was née Ge. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His younger brothers were Kun, a tribute student, and Li. His wife was née Mi. He placed sixty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 376th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Shengzong, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the prefectural Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shihan; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the fourteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather, Zhi, served as a station master; his father was Jiuchou, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shengchao, and his younger brother was Shengshi. His wife was née Gu. He placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Leshan, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Xiuzhi; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhang; his grandfather was Fu; his father was Youliang; his legal mother was née Zhao, and his birth mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jishan, a tribute student, Congshan, Jianshan, a tribute student, and Haoshan; his younger brother was Fushan. His wife was née Wu. He placed 142nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 356th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yingyuan, registered in a civilian household in Xiuning County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zizhen; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuyu; his grandfather was Xiwen; his father was Weiqin, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yingchao and Yingzheng; his younger brothers were Yingxiang, Yingfu, and Yingqiu. His wife was née Ye. He placed twenty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
王淑民〔貫陝西西安府咸寧縣民籍，四川合江縣人，國子生，治易經，字民於，行二，年三十五，七月十四日生〕。曾祖信，祖文廣，父棟，母于氏。永感下，兄添民，弟澤民、俊民〔國子生〕、新民、洽民、淳民、濬民、澄民、功民、濟民、漸民、潤民、溥民。娶葉氏。陝西鄉試第五十名，會試第三百八十九名。

鄭宗學〔貫湖廣武昌府興國州軍籍，州學生，治易經，字汝志，行二，年二十五，九月初三日生〕。曾祖淳良，祖大邦，父旦，母尹氏。具慶下，兄宗文、宗元、宗儒、宗伊、宗武、宗成，弟宗周、宗嘉、宗湯。娶徐氏。湖廣鄉試第六十三名，會試第十七名。

陳明經〔貫河南汝寧府光州民籍，儒士，治詩經，字則濟，行三，年二十三，十月初四日生〕。曾祖萬，祖汝貴，父清，母李氏。具慶下，兄明學、明倫。娶鄭氏。河南鄉試第三十八名，會試第一百十九名。

王道成〔貫四川重慶府巴縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字原恭，行一，年三十一，三月初八日生〕。曾祖武才，祖輅，父廷宣〔知州〕，母鄧氏。具慶下，弟道遠、道榮、道顯、道亨、道溥。娶李氏。四川鄉試第三十六名，會試第三百七十四名。
translation_en:
Wang Shumin, courtesy name Minyu, was registered in a civilian household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a native of Hejiang County, Sichuan. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. Second in birth order, he was thirty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Wenguang, his father Dong, and his mother née Yu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tianmin; his younger brothers were Zemin, Junmin (a student of the Directorate of Education), Xinmin, Qiamin, Chunmin, Junmin, Chengmin, Gongmin, Jimin, Jianmin, Runmin, and Pumin. The two brothers rendered Junmin were written 俊民 and 濬民 respectively. His wife was née Ye. He placed fiftieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 389th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Zongxue, courtesy name Ruzhi, was registered in a military household in Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. He was a student of the subprefectural school and specialized in the Book of Changes. Second in birth order, he was twenty-five years old, born on the third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Chunliang, his grandfather Dabang, his father Dan, and his mother née Yin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zongwen, Zongyuan, Zongru, Zongyi, Zongwu, and Zongcheng; his younger brothers were Zongzhou, Zongjia, and Zongtang. His wife was née Xu. He placed sixty-third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Mingjing, courtesy name Zeji, was registered in a civilian household in Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. He was a Confucian scholar and specialized in the Book of Odes. Third in birth order, he was twenty-three years old, born on the fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wan, his grandfather Rugui, his father Qing, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mingxue and Minglun. His wife was née Zheng. He placed thirty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Daocheng, courtesy name Yuangong, was registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. First in birth order, he was thirty-one years old, born on the eighth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Wucai, his grandfather Lu, his father Tingxuan (a Subprefect), and his mother née Deng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Daoyuan, Daorong, Daoxian, Daoheng, and Daopu. His wife was née Li. He placed thirty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 374th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張翰才〔貫山西太原府盂縣，軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字育用，行二，年三十六，十月二十四日生〕。曾祖允亨，祖通，父侃，母侯氏。具慶下，兄翰英，弟翰傑，娶陳氏。山西鄉試第五十五名，會試第一百二十三名。

杜伸〔貫湖廣黃州府黃岡縣，官籍，府學生，治禮記，字汝直，行三，年二十八，二月二十七日生〕。曾祖永琳，祖華〔鹽課司正提舉〕，父鳴陽〔知縣〕，母閔氏。具慶下，兄偉、傑〔貢士〕，弟儒、佶、修，娶汪氏。湖廣鄉試第七十七名，會試第二百五十一名。

馮笏〔貫直隸蘇州府吳縣，匠籍，長洲縣人，府學附學生，治春秋，字正伯，行三，年三十二，十月二十一日生〕。曾祖禎，祖珵，父淮〔封工部主事，加封中憲大夫、知府〕，母陸氏〔封安人，加封恭人〕。永感下，兄符〔知府〕，娶楊氏。應天府鄉試第一百八名，會試第三百六十七名。

謝師成〔貫浙江紹興府上虞縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字汝器，行五，年三十六，三月初二日生〕。曾祖克瓚，祖王，父鳴治〔教諭〕，母徐氏。嚴侍下，弟師嚴〔進士〕、師傅、師旦、師啓、師模、師正、師立、師達，娶徐氏。浙江鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百三十名。
translation_en:
Zhang Hancai, registered in Yu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuyong. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunheng, his grandfather Tong, his father Kan, and his mother née Hou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hanying and his younger brother Hanjie; his wife was née Chen. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Shen, registered in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to an official household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Ruzhi. Third in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yonglin; his grandfather Hua was Chief Superintendent of a Salt Tax Office; his father Mingyang was a Magistrate; and his mother was née Min. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wei and Jie, the latter a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Ru, Ji, and Xiu. His wife was née Wang. He ranked seventy-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Hu, registered in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was a native of Changzhou County. He was an auxiliary student at the prefectural school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zhengbo. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen and his grandfather Cheng. His father Huai had been honorifically granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Works, with the subsequent grants of Grand Master for Constitutional Service and Prefect. His mother, née Lu, had been granted the title Lady of Peace, subsequently elevated to Lady of Respect. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Fu was a Prefect; his wife was née Yang. He ranked 108th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 367th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Shicheng, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruqi. Fifth in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and born on the second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kezan, his grandfather Wang [?], his father Mingzhi, an Instructor, and his mother née Xu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Shiyan, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), Shifu, Shidan, Shiqi, Shimo, Shizheng, Shili, and Shida. His wife was née Xu. He ranked fifty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王炳衡〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣，民籍，崑山縣人，國子生，治易經，字伯欽，行一，年三十六，五月十二日生〕。曾祖銀〔贈翰林院編修〕，祖同祖〔國子監司業兼司經局校書〕，父法〔監生〕，母陸氏。慈侍下。弟炳璿〔貢士〕、炳珪〔進士〕、炳暘、炳樞、炳昂、炳權、炳魁。娶沈氏。應天府鄉試第一百三十名，會試第一百八十八名。
translation_en:
Ding Yuanfu, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jianxin; he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Yi; his father was Shixi; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yuanzheng, Yuanzhong, and Yuanjing, Superintendent of a Superintendency; his younger brothers were Yuanchun and Yuanhe. He married a woman née Lu and subsequently women née Yu and Liu. He placed 110th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 35th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Ji, registered in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Shanyin County, Zhejiang. He was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Rujin; he ranked third in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather was Tang; his father was Han; and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Tong and Dong, and his younger brother was Song. He married a woman née Wei. He placed 94th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 365th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Yao, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daoming; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the thirtieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tang, a Chief Clerk in the Nanjing Censorate; his grandfather was Huai, a County Magistrate granted the honorary title of Bureau Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his father was He, a Prefect; and his mother was née Ge, granted the title of Lady of Peace. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Can and Bing, the latter a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brother was Rong. He married a woman née An. He placed 80th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 349th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Bingheng, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Kunshan County. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Boqin; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-six years old, born on the twelfth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yin, posthumously granted the title of Hanlin Academy Junior Compiler; his grandfather was Tongzu, Director of Studies in the Directorate of Education and concurrently a Proofreader in the Editorial Service; his father was Fa, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Lu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Bingxuan, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Binggui, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); Bingyang; Bingshu; Bingang; Bingquan; and Bingkui. He married a woman née Shen. He placed 130th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Minshun, registered in a military household in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an附生 supplementary student at the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daofu; he ranked twenty-eighth in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Sili, who had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations; his grandfather was Kewan, a ninth-rank titular official; his father was Chi, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Minjie, Minqing, Mingang, Minpin, Minxian, Minyue, Minxi, and Minxiu; his younger brothers were Minzai and Minsong. His wife was née Zheng. He placed twenty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Bangjie, registered in a civilian household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an added-quota student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yingfu; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Rui, his grandfather was Mingdao, and his father was Yixian; his father's former wife was née Xu, and his mother was née Xu (許, a different surname from 徐). His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Rao. He placed twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Dajin, registered in an official household of Qingping Guard, Guizhou, and originating from Chong'an County, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bokang; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Chun, a School Instructor; his grandfather was Kui, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Constitutional Service and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father was You, Grand Master for Constitutional Service and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Bao, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Respect; his stepmother, née Lü, was granted the title Lady of Respect. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brothers were Dazhi and Dazhuang; his younger brothers were Dapeng, Dayou, Dading, and Dafu. His wife was née Sun. He placed tenth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Rushi, registered in a military household in Wuqiang County, Jinzhou Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xiaozheng; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Tai, his grandfather was Tianyou, and his father was Gen, an annual tribute student; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ruji; his younger brothers were Rulun and Ruyu. His wife was née Yu. He placed 126th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ni Tang 倪湯, courtesy name Deyuan, was registered in a civilian household in Guantao County, Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Zhong, served as Police Chief; his father, Qin, served as County Assistant Magistrate; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Lan, Ying, Huai, and Hai, and his wife was née Che. He placed seventy-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Yu 董裕, courtesy name Weiyi, was registered in a civilian household in Le’an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was ninth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jirun; his grandfather, Zhongding; his father, Yufang; his mother, née Xie; and his stepmothers, née Yao and née Liu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brother was Li, his younger brother was Bu, and his wife was née Tan. He placed thirty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Jiusi 趙九思, courtesy name Yicheng, was registered in a civilian household in Zezhou, Shanxi. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiong; his grandfather, Xi; his father, Weibang; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Jiujing, Jiuchou, Jiushao, and Jiujiang, and his wife was née Guo. He placed twenty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Guangqi 戴光啓, courtesy name Zhongsheng, was registered in a military household in Qi County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yuan, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his grandfather, Gongli, served as Police Chief; his father, Bin, served as Assistant Prefect; and his mother and stepmother were both née Xu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Guangzheng and Guangjiao, his younger brother was Guangzhao, and his wife was née Cheng. He placed nineteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張一元〔貫山東濟南府鄒平縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字鳴春，行一，年二十九，正月初三日生〕。曾祖興，祖桂〔訓導〕，父佩弦〔壽官〕，母孫氏。具慶下，弟一亨、一貞，娶劉氏。山東鄉試第四十九名，會試第三百四十五名。
translation_en:
Yin Tingjun, registered in a civilian household in Mengzi County, Lin’an Prefecture, Yunnan, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Deyong; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Ren, and his father Shilin (an honorary official for longevity); his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tingjie, Tingqing, Tingxiu, Tingjie 廷价, and Tingzuo, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed sixth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 381st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Wen, registered in a military household in Xianning County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rubei; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ao, his grandfather Wanzhang, and his father Chunyang (a tribute scholar, gongshi); his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yan, and his wife was née Zhu 祝. He placed twentieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shuai Xiang, registered in a civilian household in Anju County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Lüqing; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi, his grandfather Yuezhi, and his father Tang (a Professor in a princely establishment). His father’s former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Liu. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Ping and Jie, and his wife was née Wang. He placed forty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yiyuan, registered in a civilian household in Zouping County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mingchun; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Gui (an Assistant Instructor), and his father Peixian (an honorary official for longevity); his mother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yiheng and Yizhen, and his wife was née Liu. He placed forty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 345th in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡時化〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字惟權，行十三，年三十六，四月十七日生。〕曾祖世才，祖文琳，父華〔典史〕，母黃氏。具慶下。兄時俊，弟枋、時佐、時佑。娶李氏。浙江鄉試第六十五名，會試第十四名。

translation_en:
Yu Jiayan, courtesy name Zhangfu, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was an supplementary student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. He ranked sixth among his brothers, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the thirteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongyi; his grandfather was Wei, a ninth-rank prestige official; his father was Tianxiang; and his mother was Lady Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jiamou, and his younger brothers were Jiashan, Jiazhong, Jiabin, Jiamo, and Jiazhen. He married Lady Tao. He placed eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tingyi, courtesy name Guozhan, was registered in a civilian household in Huo Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, and was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather was Zhu; and his father was Wensheng, a Steward of Delicacies. His legal mother was Lady Guo, his stepmother was Lady Ma, and his birth mother was Lady Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tingwei. He married Lady Yao and subsequently Lady Qiao. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Shihua, courtesy name Weiquan, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. He ranked thirteenth among his brothers, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the seventeenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shicai; his grandfather was Wenlin; his father was Hua, a Chief Clerk; and his mother was Lady Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shijun, and his younger brothers were Fang, Shizuo, and Shiyou. He married Lady Li. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yu, courtesy name Dezheng, was registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather was Zhongli; his father was Cunjing; and his mother was Lady Zhu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Fang and Zhan. He married Lady Xue. He placed fifty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Zhenji, registered in a civilian household in Yishui County, Ju Subprefecture, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Kecheng; he ranked first in family order, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather Xun was a county magistrate; his grandfather Du was an annual tribute student; his father was Zhi, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhensu and Zhenye. He married a woman née Yin and subsequently a woman née Song. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Chengming, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Dengfu; he ranked first in family order, was twenty-three years old, and was born on the seventeenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather Mao was Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, posthumously awarded the title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather Yue was an adjudicator in a princely establishment; his father was Dajing, and his mother was née Liu. Parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Ruqin, Rucong, and Ruquan; his younger brothers were Ruzhong, Rujun, Qiming, and Ruxuan. He was betrothed to a woman née Wang. He placed fifty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yuntao, registered in a military household in Tangyi County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanjing; he ranked third in family order, was thirty-eight years old, and was born on the first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather was Hong, his father was Tinghuan, and his mother was née Ma. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yunpeng, a surveillance vice commissioner; Yunfeng, a student of the Directorate of Education; and Yunyan. His younger brothers were Yunlin, Yuntuan, Yunti, Yundai, and Yunlou. He married a woman née Li. He placed forty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Jian, registered in an official household of Qingzhou Guard, Shandong, was an additional student of the Yidu County school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyang; he ranked second in family order, was thirty-two years old, and was born on the second day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather was Sheng, his father Zhu was a county registrar, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ke. He married a woman née Chen. He placed fifty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 337th in the Metropolitan Examination.

朱璉〔貫江西臨江府新淦縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字文卿，行三，年三十，十月二十日生〕。曾祖德顯，祖廷翰，父士彥，前母何氏，母張氏。慈侍下，兄仁卿，娶李氏。江西鄉試第五十八名，會試第二十二名。

曹樓〔貫直隸徽州府歙縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治禮記，字世登，行二，年二十八，二月十四日生〕。曾祖觀〔貢士〕，祖禎〔貢士〕，父文修，嫡母方氏，生母張氏。嚴侍下，兄祝，娶黃氏。應天府鄉試第三名，會試第五十名。

周裔先〔貫廣東廣州府南海縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字朝采，行三，年三十二，六月二十九日生〕。曾祖景彬，祖昺，父楫，母勞氏。慈侍下，兄裔登〔知縣〕、裔遷，娶霍氏。廣東鄉試第九名，會試第二百二名。
translation_en:
Zhu Lian, registered in Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenqing. He was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dexian, his grandfather Tinghan, and his father Shiyan; his father's former wife was née He, and his mother was née Zhang. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Renqing, and his wife was née Li. He ranked fifty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yichun, registered in Shen County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shufang. He was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather Wenjie, and his father Jin; his father's former wife was née Wang, his mother was née Yu, and his stepmother was née Shi. Both his parents were deceased. His younger brother Yingchun was an Imperial University student. His wife was née Shen; he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He ranked thirty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 392nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Lou, registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county government school. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shideng. He was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the fourteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Guan and grandfather Zhen were both tribute students; his father was Wenxiu. His legal mother was née Fang, and his birth mother was née Zhang. His father alone was still living. His elder brother was Zhu, and his wife was née Huang. He ranked third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yixian, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county government school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Chaocai. He was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingbin, his grandfather Bing, his father Ji, and his mother née Lao. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Yideng, a district magistrate, and Yiqian; his wife was née Huo. He ranked ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

李梯〔貫直隸河間府任丘縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字子登，行四，年三十四，三月初五日生〕。曾祖山，祖騰，父州〔省祭官〕，母明氏。永感下，兄楠、樸、杭，娶謝氏。順天府鄉試第九十八名，會試第三百七十名。

吳中立〔貫福建建寧府浦城縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字公度，行一，年三十七，正月十三日生〕。曾祖普志，祖吉，父旦〔九品散官〕，母黃氏。嚴侍下，兄承德，弟相、中節、中行、中英、崇德、中德，娶張氏。福建鄉試第五十一名，會試第八十九名。
translation_en:
Li Dong, of Taihe County, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Qiyuan. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junxin; his grandfather, Dun, and father, Shangming, both held honorary offices conferred for longevity. His mother was née He, and his stepmother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Zhao. He placed tenth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zhenming, of Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Boji. Twenty-first in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shouning; his grandfather, Luan, was posthumously granted the title of acting Vice Director in the Ministry of Works [?]; his father, Jiusi, was a Prefect. His father's principal wife, née Zhou, held the conferred title of Lady of Peace; his birth mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Wang (汪). He placed nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Ti, of Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zideng. Fourth in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shan; his grandfather was Teng; his father, Zhou, was a sacrificial attendant [?]; his mother was née Ming. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Nan, Pu, and Hang. His wife was née Xie. He placed ninety-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 370th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhongli, of Pucheng County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Gongdu. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Puzhi; his grandfather was Ji; his father, Dan, held a ninth-rank prestige title; his mother was née Huang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Chengde; his younger brothers were Xiang, Zhongjie, Zhongxing, Zhongying, Chongde, and Zhongde. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Cui Yingqi, registered in a civilian household in Huolu County, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xianke; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Biao, his grandfather Luan, and his father Zhen, a county school instructor; his mother was née Fan. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Yingpeng, and his wife was née Huang. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhai Tingnan, registered in a military household in Hunyuan Subprefecture, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Dongshu; he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Ji, and his father Peng, an assistant magistrate; his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tinghuai, a steward; Tingwu, a tribute scholar; and Tingsong, a county registrar. His wife was née Wang. He placed fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Rui, registered in a civilian household in Quanzhou Subprefecture, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yongsi; he ranked sixth among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the thirteenth day of the intercalary first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yizhi, his grandfather Litai, and his father Xindao; his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dian, Zheng, Kai, Lun, Shen, and Ji; his younger brother was Lin. His wife was née Hu, and his subsequent wife was also née Hu. He placed seventh in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Luqing, registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daochuan; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziran, right administration vice commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his grandfather was Kai, and his father Shengjie, a county magistrate. His mother was née Zhang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Suqing, Yanqing (a county magistrate), Shouqing, Jiqing, Maoqing, and Zheqing. His wife was née Liu, and his subsequent wife was née Gao. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

漆彬〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣軍籍，府學生，治易經，字中甫，行八，年三十，十一月二十八日生〕。曾祖瓘，祖鍊，父清〔巡檢〕，母辜氏。具慶下，兄模，弟森，娶葉氏。江西鄉試第六十五名，會試第二百九十名。

武尚耕〔貫應天府溧水縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字邦聘，行十一，年二十九，十一月十四日生〕。曾祖道，祖澤，父嵠〔按察司照磨〕，前母李氏，母王氏。嚴侍下，兄尚志、尚謙、尚禮、尚儒、尚義、尚訓〔貢士〕、尚嚴〔貢士〕、尚賓〔貢士〕、尚懿〔監生〕、尚勇〔監生〕，弟尚名，娶萬氏。應天府鄉試第三名，會試第二百二十六名。

鍾昌〔貫廣東廣州府東莞縣竈籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字繼文，行一，年三十五，五月初九日生〕。曾祖英〔義官〕，祖廷偉，父禎，母王氏，繼母陳氏。具慶下，弟旦、昂、昇、昪，娶房氏。廣東鄉試第四十六名，會試第四十七名。
translation_en:
Wang Wei, registered in a military household of Zhending Guard in Zhili and a native of Qingyuan County, Shanxi, was a student of the Zhending County school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Guoguang; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Lian; his grandfather, You, received the honorary title of Prefect; his father, Fumin, was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Ren, received the title of Respectful Lady. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Zao, a Prefectural Judge, Wenjian, Wenying, and Wenyi. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed 147th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Bin, registered in a military household of Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongfu; he ranked eighth among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Guan; his grandfather was Lian; his father, Qing, was a Police Chief; and his mother was née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Mo, and his younger brother was Sen. He married a woman née Ye. He placed 65th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shanggeng, registered in a military household of Lishui County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bangpin; he ranked eleventh among his brothers, was twenty-nine years old, and was born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Dao; his grandfather was Ze; and his father, Xi, was a Records Examiner in the Provincial Surveillance Commission. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Wang. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His elder brothers were Shangzhi, Shangqian, Shangli, Shangru, Shangyi, Shangxun (a tribute student), Shangyan (a tribute student), Shangbin (a tribute student), Shangyi (a Directorate of Education student), and Shangyong (a Directorate of Education student); his younger brother was Shangming. He married a woman née Wan. He placed third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Chang, registered in a salt-producing household of Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jiwen; he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather, Ying, held an honorary official title awarded for charitable contributions; his grandfather was Tingwei; his father was Zhen; his mother was née Wang; and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dan, Ang, Sheng, and Bian. He married a woman née Fang. He placed 46th in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 47th in the Metropolitan Examination.

廖希元〔貫湖廣衡州府桂陽州藍山縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字伯才，行一，年三十二，十月三十日生〕。曾祖得舒〔七品散官〕，祖經〔州同知，封府同知〕，父文光〔府同知〕，母鄺氏〔贈宜人〕，繼母鄧氏〔封宜人〕。重慶下，兄希賢〔教諭〕，弟希夏、希稷、希夔、希化、希伯、希穆、希尹、希綬、希翰，娶何氏。湖廣鄉試第四十八名，會試第一百九十二名。

張燭〔貫山東青州府壽光縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字叔明，行三，年三十三，十二月初六日生〕。曾祖霑〔壽官〕，祖東陽〔封刑部主事〕，父標〔知府，進階亞中大夫〕，母王氏〔封安人〕，繼母劉氏。永感下，兄爕〔監生〕、烱，弟燧、榮、燿，娶隋氏。山東鄉試第六名，會試第二百九十五名。

戴洪恩〔貫直隸揚州府江都縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字子仁，行三，年三十三，十一月初七日生〕。曾祖從美，祖紀，父鯤，母唐氏。永感下，兄洪詔、洪謨，弟洪益、洪諭、洪仁、洪德、洪證，娶李氏，繼娶王氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十名，會試第二百四十四名。

傅應禎〔貫江西吉安府安福縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字思善，行三，年三十三，二月初十日生〕。曾祖伯衞，祖益，父國相，母王氏。嚴侍下，弟應祥、應禮、應瀹、應祉、應袞、應神、應祺，娶劉氏，繼娶彭氏。江西鄉試第五十八名，會試第一百二十八名。
translation_en:
Liao Xiyuan, of Lanshan County, Guiyang Subprefecture, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was registered in a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Bocai; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-two, born on the thirtieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deshu, a holder of a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather was Jing, a subprefectural vice magistrate granted the honorary title of prefectural vice prefect; and his father was Wenguang, a prefectural vice prefect. His mother, née Kuang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother, née Deng, was granted the same title. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Xixian, a school instructor; his younger brothers were Xixia, Xiji, Xikui, Xihua, Xibo, Ximu, Xiyin, Xishou, and Xihan. He married a woman née He. He placed forty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhu, of Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was registered in a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shuming; he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhan, an honorary official honored for longevity; his grandfather was Dongyang, granted the honorary title of secretary in the Ministry of Justice; and his father was Biao, a prefect promoted to the prestige title Grand Master of Lesser Rectitude. His mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady of Peace; his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xie, an Imperial University student, and Jiong; his younger brothers were Sui, Rong, and Yao. He married a woman née Sui. He placed sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Hong’en, of Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziren; he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congmei, his grandfather was Ji, and his father was Kun; his mother was née Tang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hongzhao and Hongmo; his younger brothers were Hongyi, Hongyu, Hongren, Hongde, and Hongzheng. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed 120th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Yingzhen, of Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a civilian household and was an added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Sishan; he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the tenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bowei, his grandfather was Yi, and his father was Guoxiang; his mother was née Wang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Yingxiang, Yingli, Yingyue, Yingzhi, Yinggun, Yingshen, and Yingqi. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Peng. He placed fifty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

袁實遂〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣軍籍，府學附學生，治詩經，字宗茂，行十，年四十一，十一月二十八日生〕。曾祖時重〔壽官〕，祖燁，父坤，母孫氏。嚴侍下，兄實遇、伯鼎，弟伯鼐，娶鄒氏，繼娶熊氏、郎氏。江西鄉試第五十二名，會試第三百十三名。

陳子需〔貫四川敘州府宜賓縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字以孚，行一，年三十四，八月初三日生〕。曾祖紀〔封戶部主事，贈布政司右布政使〕，祖卿〔兵部右侍郎兼都察院右僉都御史〕，父構〔布政司經歷〕，前母王氏，母劉氏。具慶下，兄燁，弟子履、子臨、子順、子萃、子升、子震、在朝、在廷，娶李氏。四川鄉試第三十名，會試第一百八十四名。

劉師魯〔貫山東萊州府掖縣軍籍，府學生，治詩經，字仲唯，行一，年三十五，九月十七日生〕。曾祖斌，祖明信〔義官〕，父祿〔訓導〕，母楊氏。具慶下，弟華魯、繼科、子端、至魯，娶張氏，繼娶侯氏、胡氏。山東鄉試第六十四名，會試第二百三名。

燕好爵〔貫山西平陽府翼城縣民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字脩夫，行六，年三十二，五月二十日生〕。曾祖佐，祖亮，父璟，母蘇氏。永感下，兄好洋、好海、好湖、好潮、好古，娶石氏。山西鄉試第四十六名，會試第二百三十五名。
translation_en:
Yuan Shisui, of military household registration in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an attached student of the prefectural school who specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zongmao; he ranked tenth in his family, was forty-one, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shizhong, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Ye; his father was Kun; and his mother was née Sun. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Shiyu and Boding, and his younger brother was Bonai. He married a woman née Zou, then successively women née Xiong and Lang. He placed fifty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and three hundred thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zixu, of civilian household registration in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the National University who specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yifu; he ranked first in his family, was thirty-four, and was born on the third day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ji, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and posthumously awarded that of Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; his grandfather was Qing, Right Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; and his father was Gou, a Registrar in the Provincial Administration Commission. His father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ye, and his younger brothers were Zilü, Zilin, Zishun, Zicui, Zisheng, Zizhen, Zaichao, and Zaiting. He married a woman née Li. He placed thirtieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shilu, of military household registration in Ye County, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the prefectural school who specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhongwei; he ranked first in his family, was thirty-five, and was born on the seventeenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather was Mingxin, an honorary official for righteousness; his father was Lu, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hualu, Jike, Ziduan, and Zhilu. He married a woman née Zhang, then successively women née Hou and Hu. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and two hundred third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Haojue, of civilian household registration in Yicheng County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was an attached student of the county school who specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiufu; he ranked sixth in his family, was thirty-two, and was born on the twentieth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zuo; his grandfather was Liang; his father was Jing; and his mother was née Su. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Haoyang, Haohai, Haohu, Haochao, and Haogu. He married a woman née Shi. He placed forty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
劉天衢〔貫湖廣黃州府蘄州廣濟縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字一登，行一，年三十，十月二十日生〕。曾祖自遠，祖尚滸，父世重，母彭氏，繼母干氏。具慶下，弟天街、天行、天豫，娶李氏。湖廣鄉試第二名，會試第九十二名。

田疇〔貫山西太原府文水縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字汝治，行二，年二十八，正月初一日生〕。曾祖廣，祖良〔壽官〕，父彥文，嫡母畢氏，生母李氏。慈侍下，兄耕，弟畇、畛、時、種、畬、豐，娶李氏。山西鄉試第三十名，會試第二百二十三名。

王來聘〔貫山西太原府壽陽縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字席珍，行一，年三十八，九月初十日生〕。曾祖雄，祖朝用，父麟〔省祭官〕，母郝氏。永感下，弟來賓、來召、來問、來薦，娶張氏，繼娶高氏、傅氏。山西鄉試第四十八名，會試第九十九名。

劉垓〔貫湖廣承天府潛江縣，民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字達可，行二，年三十，二月十八日生〕。曾祖敘和，祖巨秀〔累封工部員外郎〕，父勲〔工部員外郎，進階奉直大夫〕，前母王氏〔累贈宜人〕，母金氏〔累封宜人〕。永感下，兄日升，弟埏，娶王氏。湖廣鄉試第四名，會試第一百二十六名。
translation_en:
Liu Tianqu, registered in Guangji County, Qizhou Subprefecture, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yideng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twentieth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ziyuan, his grandfather Shanghu, and his father Shizhong. His mother was née Peng and his stepmother née Gan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tianjie, Tianxing, and Tianyu. He married a woman née Li. He placed second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Chou, registered in Wenshui County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruzhi; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the first day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Guang, his grandfather Liang (holder of an honorary title for longevity), and his father Yanwen. His father's principal wife was née Bi, and his birth mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Geng; his younger brothers were Yun, Zhen, Shi, Zhong, She, and Feng. He married a woman née Li. He placed thirtieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Laipin, registered in Shouyang County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xizhen; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xiong, his grandfather Chaoyong, and his father Lin (a sacrificial official, shengjiguan [?]). His mother was née Hao. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Laibin, Laizhao, Laiwen, and Laijian. He married a woman née Zhang, and subsequently women née Gao and née Fu. He placed forty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Gai, registered in Qianjiang County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Dake; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xuhe; his grandfather was Juxiu, who received successive honorary appointments culminating in Vice Director of a bureau in the Ministry of Works. His father was Xun, Vice Director of a bureau in the Ministry of Works, advanced to the prestige title Grand Master for Upright Service. His father's former wife, née Wang, received successive posthumous honors culminating in Lady of Suitability; his mother, née Jin, received successive honors culminating in Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Risheng and his younger brother Shan. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Sunzhen, registered in Lingui County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Gongxu; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four sui, born on the seventeenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather, Ce, was a County Magistrate posthumously granted the title of Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites; his father, Yan, was a Prefect; and his mother, née Tu, was granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Sunsheng, a Prefectural Judge, Sunji, Sunshu, Sunxian, Suncheng, Sunnian, and Sunqing. He married a woman née Hu. He placed twenty-second in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Kejiu, registered in Quwo County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Yide; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty sui, born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Tang, was a student of the Directorate of Education; his grandfather was Zi; his father was Xin; and his mother was née Qiu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Keda and Keji. He married a woman née Lu. He placed eleventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jingmin, registered in Xihua County, Chenzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was originally from Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture. He was a Xihua county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yongsi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-six sui, born on the fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Peng; his grandfather was Xun; his father, Shui, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; and his mother was née Zhu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Ximin. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed forty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yinglei, registered in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Siyu; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was thirty-six sui, born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingfu; his grandfather, Shihe, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; and his father, Ming, was a Ceremonial Officer in a princely establishment. His father's principal wife was née Xiong, his stepmother was née Liu, and his birth mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xi 熙, Xi 熈, and Mo 默 [?], the last an imperial-favor tribute student; his younger brothers were Yingri, Yingyun, and Yingsu. He married a woman née Xu. He placed fifty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

顧九思〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣民籍，府學生，治書經，字與睿，行一，年三十四，正月十九日生〕。曾祖瑢，祖𤇍〔按察司知事〕，父佐〔監生〕，母吳氏，繼母馬氏。具慶下，弟九韶、應元，娶黃氏。應天府鄉試第八十一名，會試第一百八十名。

李安仁〔貫直隸興州右屯衛軍籍，山西萬泉縣人，遷安縣學生，治易經，字體元，行二，年三十九，九月初五日生〕。曾祖通，祖昂，父臣，前母雷氏，母徐氏。具慶下，兄志仁，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第九十一名，會試第三百五十五名。

趙日新〔貫福建泉州府晉江縣軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字用甫，行一，年三十二，四月十二日生〕。曾祖瑺〔戶部郎中〕，祖信〔贈戶部主事〕，父恒〔知府〕，母王氏〔封安人〕。嚴侍下，弟日齊、日崇、日嚴、日欽，娶汪氏。福建鄉試第五名，會試第一百五十四名。
translation_en:
Wang Yunlu, courtesy name Chongru, was registered in a civilian household in Xiayi County, Guide Prefecture, Henan. An added student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wen, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Sushi; and his father was Shangzhen, a seventh-rank prestige official. His mother was née Zhu, and his stepmother née Zhang; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yunyan, a Clerk in the Imperial Medical Office; Yunluan, a tribute scholar; Yunjian; and Yunzhi. He married a woman née Xia. He placed sixteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Jiusi, courtesy name Yurui, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was 𤇍 [name reading uncertain], an Administrative Clerk in a Provincial Surveillance Commission; and his father was Zuo, an Imperial University student. His mother was née Wu, and his stepmother née Ma; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiushao and Yingyuan. He married a woman née Huang. He placed eighty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Anren, courtesy name Tiyuan, was registered in a military household of the Xingzhou Right屯 Garrison [Xingzhou You Tun Wei], in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was originally from Wanquan County, Shanxi. A student of the Qian'an county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather was Ang; and his father was Chen. His father's former wife was née Lei, and his mother née Xu; both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhiren. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed ninety-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 355th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Rixin, courtesy name Yongfu, was registered in a military household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twelfth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chang, a Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Xin, posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Heng, a Prefect. His mother was née Wang, granted the title Lady of Repose. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Riqi, Richong, Riyan, and Riqin. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zheng Binghou, registered in a commoner household in Suichang County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zizai; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangji, his grandfather Jishi, and his father Tingkang; his mother was née Ye and his stepmother née Jiang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Bingzhong and his younger brother Bingzun. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Pan. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and four hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Liangxin, registered in a salt-producing household in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xingde; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tan, his grandfather Yue, and his father Bi; his mother was née Jiang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Mao, an Office Assistant in the Court of State Ceremonial; “Service” [?], a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Gai, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Works [?—the transcribed title is irregular]; Fei, a Registrar in the Court of State Ceremonial; Lianglu; Liangji; and Liangjun. His younger brothers were Liangzou, Liangyin, and Liangyuan. He married a woman née Huang. He placed seventeenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Daji, registered in an artisan household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yunzhang; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Ang, and his father Bi; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Ding. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Guo. He placed thirty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ru Zongshun, registered in a military household of Dongsheng Right Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region, was originally from Linfen County, Shanxi. He was a Zunhua County school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zixiao; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ren, his grandfather Biao, and his father Zhang; his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zongyu and Zongtang. He married a woman née Shi. He placed eighty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Han Kai 韓鎧, courtesy name Dewei, was registered in a military household in Changping Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Song County, Henan; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fulin, his grandfather Da, his father Yi, and his mother née Li; both parents were deceased; his elder brother Xi was an annual tribute student; his wife was née Weng; he placed seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Huiqiao 劉惠喬, courtesy name Yingqian, was registered in a civilian household in Chaoyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a native of Zhenhai Guard, Fujian; he was an attached student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Kong'an, his father Weiqian, and his mother née Guo; his father was deceased and his mother living; his first wife and subsequent wife were both née Huang; he placed twelfth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Yinghe 羅應鶴, courtesy name Deming, was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siyi, his grandfather Liangsun, his father Guanzong, his legal mother née Wang, and his birth mother née Liu; both parents were living; his elder brother was Yingfeng, and his younger brothers were Yingkun, Yingpeng (a National University student), Yinghong, Yingjian, and Yinghuang; his wife was née Wang; he placed thirty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Qing 趙卿, courtesy name Ruliang, was registered in an officer household of Sizhou Guard, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered region; he was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Kuan and grandfather Wan were both company commanders; his father was Han and his mother née Ma; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Yu and Yin; his wife was née Liu; he placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

王一乾〔貫江西吉安府泰和縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字元卿，行四，年三十，正月初六日生〕。曾祖愨，祖語，父如瓚〔知府〕，前母劉氏，母廖氏。慈侍下，兄一凱、一能、一光，弟一元〔監生〕、一忱。娶郭氏，繼娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第一百七名，會試第一百五十名。

魏良知〔貫湖廣承天府京山縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字師堯，行一，年三十六，十一月十一日生〕。曾祖敬〔壽官〕，祖珍〔奉祀〕，父鷹，母胡氏。慈侍下，弟良顯、良能。娶田氏。湖廣鄉試第七十四名，會試第四十名。

詹沂〔貫直隸寧國府宣城縣匠籍，國子生，治易經，字浴之，行四，年三十五，八月十六日生〕。曾祖仲貴，祖璇，父友相，母盧氏。嚴侍下，兄淅、滾、洛，弟泮、濆、濬。娶黃氏。應天府鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百五十九名。

徐鳴鶴〔貫河南開封府杞縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字于齡，行三，年三十六，正月二十九日生〕。曾祖翀，祖周，父逵，母李氏。慈侍下，兄鳴鸞、鳴鳳，弟鳴鴈、鳴鶠、鳴謙、鳴世、鳴盛、鳴鶚。娶李氏。河南鄉試第三十二名，會試第三百九十四名。
translation_en:
Wang Yiqian, registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yuanqing; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Que; his grandfather, Yu; and his father, Ruzan, a prefect. His father’s former wife was née Liu, and his mother was née Liao. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Yikai, Yineng, and Yiguang; his younger brothers were Yiyuan, a National University student, and Yichen. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed 107th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Liangzhi, registered in a civilian household in Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Shiyao; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the eleventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, who held an honorary title for longevity; his grandfather was Zhen, a Sacrificial Officer; his father was Ying, and his mother was née Hu. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Liangxian and Liangneng. He married a woman née Tian. He placed seventy-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhan Yi, registered in an artisan household in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuzhi; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhonggui; his grandfather, Xuan; his father, Youxiang; and his mother, née Lu. His father alone was still living. His elder brothers were Xi, Gun, and Luo; his younger brothers were Pan, Fen, and Jun. He married a woman née Huang. He placed thirty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Minghe, registered in a civilian household in Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yuling; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chong; his grandfather, Zhou; his father, Kui; and his mother, née Li. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Mingluan and Mingfeng; his younger brothers were Mingyan 鳴鴈, Mingyan 鳴鶠, Mingqian, Mingshi, Mingsheng, and Ming’e. He married a woman née Li. He placed thirty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 394th in the Metropolitan Examination.

韓容〔貫山東濟南府青城縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字可受，行一，年三十二，七月初七日生〕。曾祖相〔知縣〕，祖齊〔知縣，贈南京監察御史〕，父一動〔訓導〕，母石氏。具慶下，兄章，弟芳、泉、荊、江、府、孝、忠、谷、儒、和，娶王氏。山東鄉試第十八名，會試第三百八十名。

郗據德〔貫順天府涿州，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字守之，行二，年三十三，十月十三日生〕。曾祖甫成，祖貢，父珏，母楊氏。永感下，兄惟中、惟正、志道，弟依仁、明德，娶張氏，繼娶何氏。順天府鄉試第九名，會試第二百四十八名。

唐本堯〔貫直隸松江府上海縣，竈籍，華亭縣人，國子生，治詩經，字世承，行一，年三十五，七月初九日生〕。曾祖祚〔七品散官〕，祖㑲〔贈兵部郎中〕，父自化〔監察御史〕，母楊氏〔封孺人〕。永感下，弟祖堯、紹堯、贊堯、遵堯、服堯，娶王氏，繼娶胡氏。應天府鄉試第四十八名，會試第三百五十二名。

范梅〔貫江西南昌府豐城縣，軍籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字元春，行十，年二十八，九月十五日生〕。曾祖直之，祖至泰，父楚蕘，母呂氏，繼母熊氏。慈侍下，弟梧，娶呂氏。江西鄉試第十八名，會試第八十二名。
translation_en:
Han Rong, registered in Qingcheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Keshou; he ranked first in the family order and was thirty-two, born on the seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, a County Magistrate; his grandfather was Qi, a County Magistrate posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor at Nanjing; his father was Yidong, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhang; his younger brothers were Fang, Quan, Jing, Jiang, Fu, Xiao, Zhong, Gu, Ru, and He [division of names uncertain]. His wife was née Wang. He placed eighteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 380th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xi Jude, registered in Zhuozhou, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shouzhi; he ranked second in the family order and was thirty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Fucheng, his grandfather Gong, his father Jue, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Weizhong, Weizheng, and Zhidao; his younger brothers were Yiren and Mingde. His wife was née Zhang; he subsequently married a woman née He. He placed ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Benyao, registered in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a native of Huating County. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shicheng; he ranked first in the family order and was thirty-five, born on the ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zuo, who held a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather was Nan (㑲), posthumously granted the title of Bureau Director in the Ministry of War; his father was Zihua, an Investigating Censor; and his mother was née Yang, granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Zuyao, Shaoyao, Zanyao, Zunyao, and Fuyao. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married a woman née Hu. He placed forty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 352nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Mei, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanchun; he ranked tenth in the family order and was twenty-eight, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhizhi, his grandfather Zhitai, his father Churao, his mother née Lü, and his stepmother née Xiong. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Wu, and his wife was née Lü. He placed eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

胡其高〔貫四川成都府井研縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字汝升，行一，年二十八，二月二十二日生〕。曾祖榮〔按察司僉事，加布政司叅議〕，祖洙〔壽官〕，父延春，母李氏，繼母何氏。具慶下，兄承祖〔典膳〕，弟其明、其廣、其大、文輝、汝為、文通、文耀，娶陳氏。四川鄉試第四十二名，會試第一百八十五名。
translation_en:
Wan Shide, courtesy name Boxiu, was registered in an official household at the Piantou Guard Battalion in Shanxi. He was a student of the battalion school and specialized in the Book of Changes. Ranked first in family order, he was twenty-five years old and was born on the tenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Zhen was a Battalion Commander; his grandfather Yi was an Assistant Commander; and his father Yan was a County Assistant Magistrate. His father's former wife was Lady Yang, and his mother was Lady Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shixun, and his younger brothers were Shifu and Shiming. He married Lady Yang. He placed fourteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

You Limen, courtesy name Zhongfu, was registered in a civilian household in Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. He was a county school student and specialized in the Book of Odes. Ranked second in family order, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the eighteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather was Huai, and his father was Tingfu. His mother was Lady Tian, and his stepmother was Lady Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yilu and Yili. He married Lady Bian. He placed seventy-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Yingzhao, courtesy name Mengyang, was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Changshu County. He was an additional student of the Wu County school and specialized in the Book of Documents. Ranked first in family order, he was twenty-eight years old and was born on the twenty-second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather was En, and his father was Jing. His mother was Lady Shi. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yingxi and Yingtao. He married Lady Yao. He placed eightieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Qigao, courtesy name Rusheng, was registered in a civilian household in Jingyan County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Book of Rites. Ranked first in family order, he was twenty-eight years old and was born on the twenty-second day of the second month. His great-grandfather Rong was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, with the additional title of Provincial Administration Commission Assistant Administrator; his grandfather Zhu held an honorary longevity office. His father was Yanchun, his mother was Lady Li, and his stepmother was Lady He. Both parents were living. His elder brother Chengzu was a Steward; his younger brothers were Qiming, Qiguang, Qida, Wenhui, Ruwei, Wentong, and Wenyao. He married Lady Chen. He placed forty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fang Lianggong, courtesy name Jilin, was registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a native of Panyu County. A student of the Panyu County school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. He ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the third day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yuangang; his grandfather, Song; his father, Zongyin; and his mother, née Lei. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kentang, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year, and his younger brother was Liangchen. His wife was née Liang. He placed tenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Chuxian, courtesy name Ziliang, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An additional student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. He ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yue, a prefect; his grandfather, Shan, an assistant magistrate; his father, Menglong; and his mother, née Zou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Shixian and Lixian. His wife was née Dai. He placed forty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 334th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Lai, courtesy name Yuanfu, was registered in a civilian household in Yudu County, Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the county school, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. He ranked fourth in birth order and was aged thirty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Sui; his grandfather, Yue, a sacrificial official (shengjiguan); his father, Jun; and his mother, née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Han, Dan, and Guan; his younger brothers were Hu, Zhan, Zao, and Jun. His wife was née Yi. He placed tenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lian Sanyuan, courtesy name Zixian, was registered in a civilian household in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. He ranked fourth in birth order and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Hua; his father, Xi; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Sanwei, Sanxing, and Sanpin, the last a tribute student by imperial grace. His wife was née Zheng. He placed twelfth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.
